definition_zh: 极；极点；杆；磁极；电极；对立的一端
definition_en: either end of an axis, a long slender rod, or one of two opposite extremes
core_image: 地球的自转轴从球心穿出，两端各有一个点；旁边另立一根笔直的长木杆
scene: 河边的船工撑起木筏准备过浅滩。 The boatman pushes the raft along the river with a long pole.
sceneCN: 这里 pole 指「一根细长的木杆或金属杆」（第 2 个义项：用于撑船、支撑或探测的长杆）；句意为船工用长杆把木筏撑过河面。图中可辨识物件：木筏、长杆、浅滩、河水；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Either end of the earth's axis
senses.titleCN: 地极：地球自转轴的两端
senses.definition: either of the two points where the earth's axis of rotation meets its surface
senses.definitionCN: 地球自转轴与地表相交的两个点之一
senses.example: Expeditions race to reach the South Pole.
senses.exampleCN: 探险队竞相抵达南极点。
senses.why: Greek polos named the pivot of a turning sphere; the two ends of that axis are the poles.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 polos 指旋转球体的枢轴；这条轴的两端就是极。

senses.title: A long slender rod
senses.titleCN: 杆：细长的木杆或金属杆
senses.definition: a long slender piece of wood or metal used for support, pushing or fishing
senses.definitionCN: 用于支撑、撑推或钓鱼的细长木杆或金属杆
senses.example: He planted a pole to mark the boundary.
senses.exampleCN: 他竖了一根杆子来标出边界。
senses.why: This sense has a different origin: Old English pāl 'stake' from Latin palus 'stake', not from Greek polos.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来源不同：古英语 pāl「桩」来自拉丁 palus「桩」，而非希腊 polos。

senses.title: A magnetic pole
senses.titleCN: 磁极：磁体磁力最强的两端
senses.definition: either of the two ends of a magnet where the magnetic force is concentrated
senses.definitionCN: 磁体两端磁力集中的任一端
senses.example: Like poles repel each other.
senses.exampleCN: 同名的磁极互相排斥。
senses.why: Magnetism was pictured as an axis with two ends, so those ends took the name of the earth's poles.
senses.whyCN: 磁现象被想象成一条有两端的轴，这两端便沿用了地球「极」的名称。

senses.title: An electric terminal
senses.titleCN: 电极：电源或电路的正负端
senses.definition: either of the two terminals of an electric cell or circuit
senses.definitionCN: 电池或电路的两个端子之一
senses.example: Connect the red wire to the positive pole.
senses.exampleCN: 把红线接到正极。
senses.why: Electricity inherited the two-end image from magnetism, so a battery's terminals are also poles.
senses.whyCN: 电学从磁学继承了「两端」的意象，因此电池端子也叫极。

senses.title: One of two opposite extremes
senses.titleCN: 对立的一端：两个极端之一
senses.definition: either of two opposite positions, opinions or tendencies
senses.definitionCN: 两个对立立场、观点或倾向中的任一方
senses.example: The two candidates represent opposite poles of the party.
senses.exampleCN: 两位候选人代表党内对立的两端。
senses.why: Two poles of an axis face opposite directions, which makes them a natural image for extreme opposition.
senses.whyCN: 同一轴的两极朝向相反，因此自然成为极端对立的意象。

senses.title: The pole of a circle or sphere
senses.titleCN: 极点：几何中与给定圆或球对应的点
senses.definition: a point related to a circle or sphere by a fixed geometric construction
senses.definitionCN: 与给定圆或球通过固定几何构造相联系的点
senses.example: The pole of the great circle lies on the perpendicular axis.
senses.exampleCN: 这个大圆的极点位于垂直轴上。
senses.why: Projective geometry keeps the axis-end meaning but defines the point by a relation instead of by the earth.
senses.whyCN: 射影几何保留了「轴端」之义，但用几何关系而非地球来定义这个点。

senses.title: A unit of length
senses.titleCN: 杆：英制长度单位，约五码半
senses.definition: a former unit of length equal to about five and a half yards, used in surveying
senses.definitionCN: 旧时长度单位，约合五码半，用于测量
senses.example: The field measured ten poles across.
senses.exampleCN: 这块地横量有十杆宽。
senses.why: The measuring rod itself became the unit, so a pole could mean both the stick and the length it marked.
senses.whyCN: 测量用的杆本身成了单位，因此 pole 既可指杆，也可指它所标的长度。

senses.title: A pole of a dividing cell
senses.titleCN: 细胞极：有丝分裂纺锤体的两端
senses.definition: either of the two ends of the spindle in a dividing cell, toward which chromosomes move
senses.definitionCN: 分裂细胞纺锤体的两端，染色体分别移向那里
senses.example: The spindle fibres pull chromosomes toward each pole.
senses.exampleCN: 纺锤丝把染色体拉向两极。
senses.why: A dividing cell behaves like a tiny sphere with an axis, so its spindle ends are called poles.
senses.whyCN: 分裂的细胞像带轴的小球，因此纺锤体两端被称为极。

intro.en: Pole has two separate origins that happen to share a spelling: the geographic and magnetic pole from Greek polos 'axis', and the rod from Old English pāl 'stake', from Latin palus. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pole 有两个恰好同形的来源：地理与磁学的「极」来自希腊 polos「轴」，而「杆」来自古英语 pāl「桩」，再上溯拉丁 palus。年代均为约数。

items.en: Polos meant 'pivot, axis, end of an axis'. Its deeper origin is not established, and links to a 'turn' root are hypotheses.
items.cn: polos 意为「枢轴、轴、轴端」。其更深来源未得到证明，与「转动」词根的联系属假说。

items.en: Latin polus 'pole, especially of the heavens' was borrowed from Greek and passed into English as pole.
items.cn: 拉丁 polus「极，尤指天极」借自希腊语，后进入英语作 pole。

items.en: The rod sense comes from Old English pāl 'stake, post', borrowed from Latin palus 'stake'. Palus 'stake' is a different word from palus 'marsh'.
items.cn: 「杆」义来自古英语 pāl「桩、柱」，借自拉丁 palus「桩」。palus「桩」与 palus「沼泽」是两个不同的词。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the ends of a magnet were called poles by analogy with the earth's axis.
items.cn: 16 世纪起，磁体两端因类比地球轴端而被称为极。

items.en: By the seventeenth century 'poles apart' and 'opposite poles' extended the axis image to opinions and positions.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，poles apart 与 opposite poles 把轴端意象扩展到观点与立场。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates only): the exact first English use of the unit of length and of the cell-biology sense is not recorded; the two roots themselves are well documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：长度单位与细胞生物学义在英语中的确切首见年代未见记录；两个词根本身都有充分文献。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound like pole; group two holds rods, ends and extremes.
note.cn: 第一组是外形或读音接近 pole 的词；第二组是关于杆、端点与极端的词。

entries.definition: A survey of opinions or a vote; it sounds identical to pole but has no axis or rod meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 指民意调查或投票；与 pole 同音，但没有轴或杆的意思。

entries.definition: Light in colour, or a boundary stake; the vowel is different from pole.
entries.definitionCN: 颜色浅的，或指界桩；元音与 pole 不同。

entries.definition: A small body of water or a shared fund; the vowel is long and different.
entries.definitionCN: 小水塘或共用资金；元音更长且不同。

entries.definition: A small burrowing animal or a spot on the skin; it shares the ending but not the meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 穴居小动物或皮肤上的痣；词尾相同而意义无关。

entries.definition: A strong upright piece of timber or metal fixed in the ground; a pole may be movable and thinner.
entries.definitionCN: 固定在地上的坚固立木或金属柱；pole 可能更细且可移动。

entries.definition: A slim straight bar of wood or metal; pole is longer and often used for pushing.
entries.definitionCN: 细直的木条或金属条；pole 更长，常用于撑推。

entries.definition: A heavy horizontal timber or metal bar that carries a load; it is structural, unlike a simple pole.
entries.definitionCN: 承重的粗大水平木梁或金属梁；它是结构件，不同于普通杆。

entries.definition: The furthest point or most intense degree; a pole is one of two extremes facing each other.
entries.definitionCN: 最远的点或最强的程度；pole 是彼此相对的两个极端之一。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: two real roots, real magnetism and real surveying, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实词根、真实的磁学与真实的测量，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Geographic pole comes from Greek polos 'axis'; rod pole comes from Latin palus 'stake'. Same spelling, different roots.
normal.cn: 地理的 pole 来自希腊 polos「轴」；杆义的 pole 来自拉丁 palus「桩」。同形不同源。

normal.en: The North Pole and South Pole are the two ends of the earth's rotation axis.
normal.cn: 北极与南极是地球自转轴的两端。

normal.en: Like magnetic poles repel, unlike poles attract.
normal.cn: 同名磁极相斥，异名磁极相吸。

normal.en: A battery has a positive pole and a negative pole.
normal.cn: 电池有正极与负极。

normal.en: Poles apart means as far apart as the two ends of an axis.
normal.cn: poles apart 意为像轴的两端那样相距极远。

abstract.en: Picture two flags planted at the ends of a long straight road.
abstract.cn: 想象一条笔直长路的两端各插一面旗。

abstract.en: Picture a see-saw with one end up and the other down.
abstract.cn: 想象一块跷跷板，一端翘起、一端落下。

abstract.en: Picture a tent held up by one simple straight stick.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶帐篷只靠一根笔直的棍子撑起。

examples.en: The expedition reached the North Pole by dog sled.
examples.cn: 探险队乘狗拉雪橇抵达北极。

examples.en: He vaulted over the fence with a long pole.
examples.cn: 他用一根长杆撑过栅栏。

examples.en: Their political views are poles apart.
examples.cn: 他们的政治观点截然相反。

dict_mnemonic.text: pole 有两个来源：地理「极」来自希腊轴心，长「杆」来自拉丁木桩；同形两义 → 极、杆

root: 地理与磁学的 pole 来自希腊 polos「轴」经拉丁 polus；杆义的 pole 来自古英语 pāl「桩」，再上溯拉丁 palus「桩」。两源同形异义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses divide between an axis and a rod: the earth's two ends, a long stick, magnetic and electric terminals, opposite extremes, a geometric point, a unit of length, and the ends of a dividing cell.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分属「轴」与「杆」两条线：地球两端、长杆、磁极与电极、对立极端、几何极点、长度单位，以及分裂细胞的两极。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an axis emerging from a turning sphere at two ends, beside a single straight rod.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条轴从旋转球体的两端穿出，旁边另立一根笔直的长杆。

branches.en: TWO ENDS: earth, magnet and battery all concentrate their force at a pair of ends.
branches.cn: 两端：地球、磁体与电池都把力集中在成对的两端。

branches.en: THE ROD: a stick becomes a tool and then a unit of length.
branches.cn: 杆：一根棍子成为工具，再成为长度单位。

branches.en: OPPOSITION: two ends facing away become a picture of extreme disagreement.
branches.cn: 对立：两端背向而居，成为极端分歧的图景。

branches.en: GEOMETRY: a circle or sphere defines a matching point on its axis.
branches.cn: 几何：圆或球在它的轴上定义一个对应的点。

branches.en: CELL: a dividing cell's spindle has two ends that pull chromosomes apart.
branches.cn: 细胞：分裂细胞的纺锤体有两端，把染色体拉向两边。

intro.en: Pole carries two Latin roots that look alike in English: polus 'axis' and palus 'stake'. Compounds such as flagpole come from the rod, while polar and polarity come from the axis.
intro.cn: pole 在英语中合并了两个外形相近的拉丁词根：polus「轴」与 palus「桩」。flagpole 等复合词来自「杆」，polar 与 polarity 来自「轴」。

latinIntro.en: Greek polos 'axis' gives Latin polus, English pole, polar and polarity; Latin palus 'stake' gives Old English pāl, English pole 'rod' and palisade.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 polos「轴」衍生拉丁 polus、英语 pole、polar 与 polarity；拉丁 palus「桩」衍生古英语 pāl、英语 pole「杆」与 palisade。

items.example: The Latin word entered English as pole.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词进入英语作 pole。

items.example: The South Pole is colder than the coast.
A different Latin word from polus.
items.exampleCN: 这是与 polus 不同的拉丁词。

items.example: A palisade surrounded the old fort.
items.exampleCN: 旧堡垒四周有木桩栅栏。

items.example: The flagpole stands in the square.
She cleared the bar in the pole-vault.
items.exampleCN: 她在撑杆跳中越过了横杆。

definition_en: the smallest living unit of an animal or plant, a small room such as a prison room, or a device that stores electric power
core_image: 一个四面封闭的小格子
scene: 显微镜下能看到微小的结构。 Each cell in the sample had a dark centre.
sceneCN: 这里 cell 指「细胞」（第 1 个义项：生物体最小的生命单位）；句意是样本里的每个细胞都有一个深色的中心。

senses.title: The basic unit of life
senses.definition: the smallest part of a living thing that can carry out the processes of life
senses.definitionCN: 生物体中能进行生命活动的最小单位
senses.example: A red blood cell carries oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 红细胞负责运送氧气。
senses.why: Early microscopists saw tiny walled compartments and borrowed the word for a small room.
senses.whyCN: 早期显微镜学家看到一个个有壁的小隔间，就借用了表示小房间的词。

senses.title: A small closed room
senses.definition: a small room, especially one in a prison or a monastery
senses.definitionCN: 小型房间，尤指监狱或修道院中的
senses.example: The prisoner paced his narrow cell.
senses.exampleCN: 犯人在狭窄的牢房里来回踱步。
senses.why: This is the original sense: a small enclosed room, from Latin cella.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义：拉丁语 cella 所指的小型封闭房间。

senses.title: A unit that stores electric power
senses.definition: a container of chemicals that produces electricity, or one unit of a larger battery
senses.definitionCN: 通过化学物质产生电的容器，或电池组中的一节
senses.example: The torch needs a new cell.
senses.exampleCN: 手电筒需要换一节电池。
senses.why: Each battery unit is a sealed compartment, so the room word fits the small power box.
senses.whyCN: 每个电池单元都是密封的小格，于是房间用词正好套在这只电源小盒上。

intro.en: Cell comes from Latin cella, a small room, and every later sense keeps the idea of a closed compartment.
intro.cn: cell 来自拉丁语 cella（小房间），后面每个义项都保留封闭小格的意思。

items.en: Cella meant a small room, a storeroom or a shrine chamber.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cella 指小房间、储藏室或神庙内室。

items.en: Celle named a small room, especially a monk's chamber.
items.cn: 古法语 celle 指小房间，尤指修士的居室。

items.en: Cell covers small rooms in monasteries and prisons.
items.cn: 中古英语 cell 涵盖修道院和监狱的小室。

items.en: Microscopy applies the word to the tiny compartments seen in living tissue.
items.cn: 十七世纪显微镜学把该词用到活体组织中的微小隔间上。

items.en: Electricity adds the battery sense, and compounds such as cell phone spread the word further.
items.cn: 电学又添上电池义，cell phone 等复合词进一步推广该词。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the room root through its derivatives, while the meaning group lists other enclosed spaces.
note.cn: 形近组沿房间词根经派生词展开，近义组列出其他封闭空间。

entries.definition: made of cells, or relating to mobile phones
entries.definitionCN: 由细胞组成的，或与移动电话有关的

entries.definition: a person who shares a prison cell
entries.definitionCN: 同住一间牢房的人

entries.definition: the substance forming plant cell walls
entries.definitionCN: 构成植物细胞壁的物质

entries.definition: a part of a building enclosed by walls
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物中被墙围起的一部分

entries.definition: a large room used for a special purpose
entries.definitionCN: 用于特定用途的大房间

entries.definition: one of several separate sections
entries.definitionCN: 若干分隔部分中的一格

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the little-room root, the blood and prison phrases and the -ular ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用小房间词根、血液与监狱搭配以及 -ular 词尾。

normal.en: Cell is simply Latin cella, a small room, and every sense is still a little box.
normal.cn: cell 就是拉丁语 cella（小房间），每个义项都还是一个小盒子。

normal.en: A prison cell and a biological cell share one shape: a wall around a small space.
normal.cn: 牢房与生物细胞共享一个形状：围住小空间的墙。

normal.en: Cellular means made of cells, and also names the mobile phone network built from small areas.
normal.cn: cellular 意为由细胞组成，也指由小区域构成的移动电话网。

normal.en: Cellmate is cell plus mate, the person sharing that small room.
normal.cn: cellmate 是 cell 加 mate，同住那间小室的人。

normal.en: The plural cells is regular, and the word stays one syllable throughout.
normal.cn: 复数 cells 变化规则，整词始终只有一个音节。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny walled box seen through a microscope lens.
abstract.cn: 想象透过显微镜镜片看到的一个微小带壁盒子。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow stone room with one high window.
abstract.cn: 想象一间窄小的石屋，只有一扇高窗。

abstract.en: Picture a small metal cylinder sliding into a torch.
abstract.cn: 想象一节小金属筒滑进手电筒。

examples.en: The disease attacks healthy cells in the blood.
examples.cn: 这种病攻击血液中的健康细胞。

examples.en: He spent three nights in a police cell.
examples.cn: 他在警局牢房里待了三晚。

examples.en: This lamp runs on a single cell.
examples.cn: 这盏灯只用一节电池。

dict_mnemonic.text: cell 读音短促，像把小盒子「塞」进口袋：细胞、牢房、电池都是一个个封闭的小格。

root: 源自拉丁语 cella（小房间、储藏室），经古法语 celle 进入英语，由房间义扩展到生物细胞与电池单元。

sensesIntro.en: A small room gives the prison sense, the microscope borrows the shape for life, and electricity borrows it again for power units.
sensesIntro.cn: 小房间给出牢房义，显微镜借这个形状指生命单位，电学又借它指电源单元。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small space shut in by walls.
core.cn: 核心意象：四面被墙围住的小空间。

branches.en: Monastery and prison rooms keep the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 修道院与监狱的房间保留最古老的义项。

branches.en: Microscopy transfers the walled box to living tissue.
branches.cn: 显微镜学把带壁盒子转移到活体组织上。

branches.en: Electricity seals chemicals inside a small cylinder.
branches.cn: 电学把化学物质封在小圆筒里。

branches.en: Both are tiny enclosed units separated from neighbours.
branches.cn: 两者都是与邻居隔开的小封闭单元。

branches.en: Both senses keep the physical container visible.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留了可见的实体容器。

intro.en: Cell builds adjectives and nouns with -ular, -ulose and the compound mate.
intro.cn: cell 用 -ular、-ulose 以及复合成分 mate 构成形容词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin cella also gives cellar and the first element of cemetery.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cella 也给出 cellar，以及 cemetery 的前半部分。

items.meaning: a small room or living unit

items.example: His cellmate taught him to read.
Her cell phone rang in the meeting.
The prison cell had no window.
Cella is the source of cell.
items.exampleCN: cella 是 cell 的来源。

latinEntries.exampleCN: cella 也是 cellar 的来源。

definition_en: to put a dead body into the ground
core_image: 土坑旁堆起的一座新坟
scene: 狗在院子角落刨个不停。 The dog buried the bone in the garden.
sceneCN: 这里 bury 是「掩埋」（第 2 个义项：把东西埋进土里）；句意是狗把骨头埋在院子里。

collocations.phrase: bury one's face in one's hands

senses.title: To place a body in the ground
senses.definition: to put a dead person or animal into the earth
senses.definitionCN: 把死去的或动物放入土中
senses.example: They buried him beside the old church.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把他葬在旧教堂旁。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, tied to funeral custom.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，与丧葬习俗相关。

senses.title: To cover with earth
senses.definition: to cover something with soil or another material
senses.definitionCN: 用土或其他材料把东西盖住
senses.example: The dog buried the bone in the garden.

intro.cn: bury 是古老的日耳曼词，意为把东西放进土里。

items.cn: byrgan 意为埋葬遗体。

items.cn: bury 扩展到把物品埋进土里。

items.en: Burial named the funeral ceremony.
items.cn: burial 指葬礼仪式。

items.en: Burying oneself in study meant total attention.

items.en: bury covers funerals, hidden things and deep attention.
items.cn: 如今 bury 涵盖葬礼、埋藏与专注。

normal.en: Dogs bury bones to save them.

normal.en: Buried in work means very busy.

normal.en: Bury the past and move on.

abstract.en: See a head bent low over a book.

definition_zh: 经由；经过（某地）；通过、借助（某人或某手段）
definition_en: by way of a place, or by means of a person or method
core_image: 一条路线在纸上转弯，绕过一座山，最后才到达目的地
scene: 邮件在三个城市之间转了一圈，最后才落到桌上。 We flew to Rome via Zurich.
sceneCN: 这里 via 是「经由某地」（第 1 个义项：路线经过某地）；句意为我们先飞到苏黎世，再转去罗马。那条绕过山再到的路线，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 介词：经由、经过；通过、借助

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「高架桥」，与 via 同源于拉丁语 via「道路」
动词，义为「偏离」，同源于拉丁语 via
形容词，义为「明显的」，字面义为「在路上迎面遇上」，同根
形容词，义为「琐碎的」，字面义为「三岔路口的」，同根

senses.title: By way of a place
senses.titleCN: 经由某地：路线经过而不停留
senses.definition: travelling through a place on the way to another
senses.definitionCN: 在前往另一地途中经过某地
senses.example: We flew to Rome via Zurich.
senses.exampleCN: 我们先飞到苏黎世，再转去罗马。
senses.why: Latin via is a road; the preposition simply names the road taken without claiming a stop.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 via 就是道路；这个介词只说走的是哪条路，并不表示停下来。

senses.title: By means of
senses.titleCN: 通过、借助：靠某种手段完成
senses.definition: by means of a particular method, person or service
senses.definitionCN: 通过某种方法、人或服务实现
senses.example: We sent the documents via email to save time.
senses.exampleCN: 为了省时间，我们通过电子邮件发了文件。
senses.why: The road becomes a figure of speech: the channel that carries the action.
senses.whyCN: 道路变成了比喻：承载这个动作的通道。

senses.title: Through an intermediary
senses.titleCN: 经某人转手：不直接对接
senses.definition: through a person or office acting in between
senses.definitionCN: 通过居间的人或机构
senses.example: The message reached him via his assistant.
senses.exampleCN: 消息通过他的助理传到了他那里。
senses.why: The route now runs through a person rather than through a town.
senses.whyCN: 路线这次穿过的是一个人，而不是一座城镇。

senses.title: Through a route or medium
senses.titleCN: 通过某一路径或媒介：抽象通道
senses.definition: through a particular route, path or medium
senses.definitionCN: 通过特定路径或媒介
senses.example: Data travels via underground cables to the other building.
senses.exampleCN: 数据经地下电缆传到另一栋楼。
senses.why: A cable is a road for electricity, and the word applies without any change of form.
senses.whyCN: 电缆是电的道路，这个词不再变形就直接用上了。

intro.en: Via is the Latin noun for road, taken whole into English and pressed into service as a preposition.
intro.cn: via 是拉丁语里表示「道路」的名词，整块进入英语后被用作介词。

items.en: The noun via meant a road, way or street, and also a method.
items.cn: 名词 via 意为道路、路径，也可指方法。

items.en: In phrases such as via Appia the ablative already worked as by way of, a road name in use.
items.cn: 在 via Appia 这类短语里，这个夺格形式已经带有「经……路」的意味。

items.en: English borrowed via in the eighteenth century as a preposition of route.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入 via，用作表路线的介词。

items.en: Rail, aviation and postal writing spread it through travel timetables.
items.cn: 铁路、航空与邮政文书把它普及到旅行时刻表里。

items.en: Modern usage adds the abstract sense, so documents now travel via email.
items.cn: 现代用法增添了抽象含义，于是文件可以通过邮件旅行。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin road root; the near-meaning group holds prepositions of route and means.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁「道路」词根；近义组收表示路线与手段的介词。

entries.definition: A road carried over a valley; literally a road leader.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「高架桥」，字面即「引路之桥」。

entries.definition: To leave the road; hence to stray.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「偏离」，字面即离开道路。

entries.definition: Literally lying in the road, hence plain to see.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明显的」，字面即「在路中遇到」。

entries.definition: Of a crossroads, hence common and slight.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「琐碎的」，由「三岔路口」引申为常见而轻微。

entries.definition: By way of, inside and out the other side.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「穿过」，从一头进、另一头出。

entries.definition: By means of, or past a point on a route.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「靠、经」，也可指路过某点。

entries.definition: In every part, stronger than via.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「遍及」，比 via 更强。

entries.definition: Following the length of a road or river.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「沿着」，顺着路或河的长度走。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the literal road and the modern habits of travel and mail.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用字面上的「道路」，以及现代出行与邮件的习惯。

normal.en: Via is Latin for road, and roads explain the word.
normal.cn: via 是拉丁语的「道路」，道路解释了它。

normal.en: Fly via Paris means Paris is on the way, not the destination.
normal.cn: fly via Paris 指巴黎在途中，不是目的地。

normal.en: Send it via email means the message takes a digital road.
normal.cn: send it via email 指消息走了一条数字的路。

normal.en: Obvious, deviate and trivial all come from the same road word.
normal.cn: obvious、deviate、trivial 都出自同一个「道路」词。

normal.en: Via does not mean in: you do not stop there for long.
normal.cn: via 不等于 in：你不在那里久留。

abstract.en: Via names the path rather than the place: it tells you how the thing got here.
abstract.cn: via 命名的是路径而非地点：它告诉你东西是怎么过来的。

abstract.en: Anything that moves needs a road, so the word stretches to cables, satellites and people.
abstract.cn: 凡会动的东西都需要一条路，于是这个词扩展到电缆、卫星和人。

abstract.en: To name the route is already to hint at the motive, which is why the same word covers means.
abstract.cn: 说出路线已经在暗示成因，所以同一个词也能表示手段。

examples.en: We returned home via the coast road.
examples.cn: 我们沿着海边公路回家。

examples.en: Please send your application via the website.
examples.cn: 请通过网站提交申请。

examples.en: He learned the news via a friend in the office.
examples.cn: 他从办公室的一位朋友那里得到这个消息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外啊」——外啊，外面这条路经过咱们这儿：经由

root: 直接来自拉丁语名词 via「道路、方法」，十八世纪起在英语中作介词使用；同根词有 viaduct、deviate、obvious、trivial。

sensesIntro.en: Via travels from a real road, to a method, to a person in between, to an abstract channel.
sensesIntro.cn: via 从真实的道路出发，走到方法、居间的人，再到抽象的通道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line on a map that bends around a hill before reaching the mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上一条线绕过小山，才到目的地。

branches.en: ROUTE LINE: a place passed on the way.
branches.cn: 路线线：途中经过的地点。

branches.en: METHOD LINE: the means by which it is done.
branches.cn: 方法线：办成事所借助的手段。

branches.en: PEOPLE LINE: a message relayed by someone else.
branches.cn: 人际线：由别人转达的消息。

branches.en: CABLE LINE: an abstract path or medium.
branches.cn: 线路线：抽象的路径或媒介。

branches.en: CONTRAST: via names the way, in names the place.
branches.cn: 对照线：via 说路，in 说地。

intro.en: Via has no affixes, but the Latin noun it comes from hides inside several English words.
intro.cn: via 没有词缀，但构成它的拉丁名词藏在好几个英语词里。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun via, road, survives in viaduct, deviate, obvious and trivial.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 via「道路」残留在 viaduct、deviate、obvious、trivial 里。

items.example: It forms deviate, to leave the road.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 deviate，即离开道路。

items.example: It forms obvious, in the way.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 obvious，即在路中遇到。

items.example: It forms trivial, of three roads.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 trivial，即三岔路口的。

definition_en: an organized group, or a connection between things
core_image: 一群人围着同一张桌子坐下
scene: 街角的老楼门口挂起一块新牌子。 The residents formed an association to save the building.
sceneCN: 这里 association 是「协会」（第 1 个义项：为共同目的组成的团体）；句意是居民们成立协会来保住这栋楼。

senses.title: Organized group
senses.definition: an organized group of people with a shared purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为共同目的组织起来的一群人
senses.example: The residents formed an association to save the building.
senses.exampleCN: 居民们成立协会来保住这栋楼。
senses.why: Association is associate plus -ion, so a verb meaning 'to join as companions' becomes the body of companions who have joined, that is, an organized group.
senses.whyCN: association 是 associate 加 -ion，把「结为同伴」的动词变成结成伴的那一群人，也就是有组织的团体。

senses.title: Connection or mental link
senses.definition: a connection between two things, including one made in the mind
senses.definitionCN: 两件事之间的关联，也包括脑中的联想
senses.example: The study found an association between sleep and memory.
senses.exampleCN: 研究发现了睡眠与记忆之间的关联。
senses.why: The same joining, once it is between facts or ideas rather than people, becomes a link that can be measured or merely felt in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「结伴」如果发生在事实或观念之间而不是人之间，就成了可以被测量或只在脑中感到的关联。

intro.en: Association is the noun of joining, used both for groups of people and for links between things.
intro.cn: association 是表示「结合」的名词，既指人的团体，也指事物之间的关联。

items.en: socius meant 'companion'.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴」。

items.en: associare meant 'to join together'.
items.cn: associare 意为「结合在一起」。

items.en: Old French associer kept the sense of uniting.
items.cn: 古法语 associer 保留「联合」之义。

items.en: Association named a guild or a body of people.
items.cn: association 指行会或一群有组织的人。

items.en: Psychology gave the word its sense of a mental link.
items.cn: 心理学赋予它「脑中联想」的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the associ stem; the near-meaning group names groups and links.
note.cn: 形近组共享 associ 词干；近义组是表示团体与关联的词。

entries.definition: to join or connect
entries.definitionCN: 联系；交往

entries.definition: relating to people together
entries.definitionCN: 社会的

entries.definition: to separate
entries.definitionCN: 使分离

entries.definition: an organized body
entries.definitionCN: 组织

entries.definition: a link between things
entries.definitionCN: 关联

entries.definition: a tie between two things
entries.definitionCN: 联系

normalIntro.en: An association can be a room full of members or a thread between two facts.
normalIntro.cn: association 可以是一屋子会员，也可以是两个事实之间的一根线。

normal.en: The ending -tion marks the noun built on associate.
normal.cn: 结尾 -tion 标记由 associate 构成的名词。

normal.en: In association with means working together with another body.
normal.cn: in association with 指与另一机构合作。

normal.en: In research writing it often means a statistical link.
normal.cn: 在研究写作里它常指统计上的关联。

normal.en: Stress the fourth syllable: as-so-ci-A-tion.
normal.cn: 重音在第四个音节。

normal.en: Do not drop the second i in spelling.
normal.cn: 拼写时不要漏掉第二个 i。

abstract.en: See a long table with name cards around it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，四周摆着名牌。

abstract.en: See a thin line drawn between two words on a page.
abstract.cn: 想象书页上两个词之间画了一条细线。

abstract.en: See a key ring holding many keys of one building.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋楼的许多钥匙串在一个环上。

examples.en: The residents formed an association to save the building.
examples.cn: 居民们成立协会来保住这栋楼。

examples.en: The study found an association between sleep and memory.
examples.cn: 研究发现了睡眠与记忆之间的关联。

examples.en: She works in association with a local charity.
examples.cn: 她与一家本地慈善机构合作。

root: 由 associate 加 -ion 构成；associate 源自拉丁语 socius「同伴」，因此 association 既指因共同目的结成的人群，也指事物之间乃至脑中的关联。

sensesIntro.en: People joining and ideas joining share one noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 人结成伴与观念结成伴，共用一个名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: separate names written on one membership list.
core.cn: 核心意象：各自的名字写在同一张会员名册上。

branches.en: a trade association
branches.cn: 行业协会

branches.en: a residents' association
branches.cn: 居民协会

branches.en: an association between sleep and memory
branches.cn: 睡眠与记忆的关联

branches.en: a strong association
branches.cn: 紧密的联系

branches.en: in association with a charity
branches.cn: 与慈善机构合作

intro.en: The -ion ending turns the verb of joining into the thing or state that results.
intro.cn: 结尾 -ion 把表示结合的动词变成结合后的事物或状态。

latinIntro.en: The root soci, 'companion', also underlies society and sociology.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 soci「同伴」也是 society 与 sociology 的来源。

definition_zh: 托盘；盘子；浅盘；文件盘；沙盘
definition_en: a flat, shallow container with a raised edge for carrying or holding things
core_image: 托在腕上的浅盘：四边微微翘起，稳稳托住一切
scene: 食堂打饭窗口前，同学们端着空盘子依次排队： At the canteen window students carried trays full of food, queuing slowly towards the till.
sceneCN: 这里 tray 是「托盘」（第 1 个义项：带边沿的浅盘）；句意是学生端着装饭菜的餐盘排队。

derivatives.zh: 由 tray 加 -ful 构成，义为「一盘之量」（罕用）
由 ash 加 tray 构成，义为「烟灰缸」
与 tray 常搭配的名词短语，义为「点心烤盘」

senses.title: A flat shallow container with a raised rim
senses.definition: a flat piece of material with raised edges, used for carrying or holding things
senses.definitionCN: 边缘翘起的扁平容器，用于托举或盛放
senses.example: The waiter balanced a tray of drinks above the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 侍者把盛满饮料的托盘稳稳举过人群。
senses.why: The core image is a shallow plate with lifted edges holding everything steady.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是四边翘起的浅盘，把一切稳稳托住。

senses.title: An open compartment for papers or small items
senses.definition: an open container on a desk or in a machine for papers or parts
senses.definitionCN: 桌上或机器里放文件或小件的敞口容器
senses.example: Letters for signature wait in the in tray on her desk.
senses.exampleCN: 待签的信件躺在她桌上的收文盘里。
senses.why: The rim that once held drinks now holds papers and parts.
senses.whyCN: 当年托住饮料的边沿，如今托住文件与零件。

senses.title: A tray used in cooking or science
senses.definition: a flat metal dish for baking, or a shallow dish for laboratory work
senses.definitionCN: 烘烤用的扁平金属盘，或实验室用的浅盘
senses.example: Line the baking tray with paper before the cookies go in.
senses.exampleCN: 饼干入炉前先在烤盘上铺纸。
senses.why: Wherever things must be carried flat and level, a tray appears.
senses.whyCN: 凡需水平平稳盛放之物，便有 tray 的用武之地。

intro.en: Tray comes from Old English treg, træg, a wooden board or runner, related to tree and timber; the shallow board for holding things became the tray.
intro.cn: tray 来自古英语 treg/træg「木板、滑条」，与 tree、timber 同族；承物的浅木板遂成今日的托盘。

items.en: treg or træg meant a wooden board or slope-shaped runner.
items.cn: 古英语 treg/træg 意为木板或斜面滑条。

items.en: Generally related to the Germanic word family of tree and timber.
items.cn: 一般认为属日耳曼语族 tree、timber 词族。

items.en: tray named shallow boards for carrying food.
items.cn: 中古英语 tray 指端送食物的浅木板。

items.en: Extended to desks, machines, ovens, and laboratories.

senses.definition: the process by which a living thing becomes larger

senses.example: The growth of the young tree needs sunlight.

abstract.en: Growth asks for room before it asks for thanks.

definition_zh: 可移动的；流动的；手机；活动雕塑
definition_en: able to move or be moved; changing place or rank easily; also a phone carried by the user and a hanging sculpture turned by air
core_image: 一只箱子装上小轮，人一推就走，位置随时能换
scene: 夜里的车站出口挤满人，一个年轻人拖着箱子，另一只手举着小屏幕贴在耳边。 She answered her mobile while dragging a suitcase through the crowd.
sceneCN: 这里是「手机」（第 3 个义项：随身携带的移动电话）；句意为她一边拖着行李箱穿过人群，一边接听手机。图中可辨识物件：滚轮行李箱、亮着的屏幕、车站出口的灯。

pos.zh: 可移动的；流动的；变动灵活的

derivatives.zh: 由 mobile 去 e 加 -ity 构成，义为「流动性；移动能力」
由 mobile 加 -ize 构成，义为「动员；组织起来行动」
由希腊语 autos（自己）加 mobile（可动的）构成，义为「汽车」
由否定前缀 im- 加 mobile 构成，义为「不能移动的；静止的」

senses.title: Able to move or be moved
senses.definition: able to move by itself, or able to be moved from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 能自行移动，或能被从一个地方搬到另一个地方
senses.example: A mobile desk lets you work in either room.
senses.exampleCN: 一张可移动的书桌让你在哪个房间都能工作。
senses.why: Latin mobilis was built from movere, to move, plus -bilis, able to be, so the adjective literally says able to move before it ever says anything about phones.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mobilis 由 movere（移动）加 -bilis（能……的）构成，所以这个形容词字面上先说「能动」，比它用来指手机要早得多。

senses.title: Changing place or rank easily
senses.definition: able or likely to change job, home or social position
senses.definitionCN: 能够或容易更换工作、住所或社会地位的
senses.example: A mobile workforce follows the work wherever it appears.
senses.exampleCN: 流动的劳动力会跟着工作机会走。
senses.why: If a thing can be moved, people and jobs can move too, so English extended the same adjective to labour, to families and to whole societies that do not stay put.
senses.whyCN: 如果一样东西能被搬动，人和工作也能移动，于是英语把这同一个形容词扩展到劳动力、家庭乃至不断变动的社会。

senses.title: A telephone carried with you
senses.definition: a telephone that works through a network of radio cells and is carried by its user
senses.definitionCN: 依靠蜂窝式无线电网络工作、由使用者随身携带的电话
senses.example: She answered her mobile while dragging a suitcase through the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 她一边拖着行李箱穿过人群，一边接听手机。
senses.why: A phone that is not tied to a desk or a wall socket inherits the oldest sense of the adjective, and English simply dropped the noun phone and kept the describing word.
senses.whyCN: 不拴在桌上或墙上的电话继承了形容词最老的意思；英语省掉了 phone 这个名词，只留下那个起描述作用的词。

senses.title: A hanging sculpture turned by air
senses.definition: a sculpture of balanced parts that hang and turn with air currents
senses.definitionCN: 由平衡的部件悬挂而成、随气流转动的雕塑
senses.example: A metal mobile turned slowly above the hospital bed.
senses.exampleCN: 一件金属活动雕塑在病床上方缓缓转动。
senses.why: Alexander Calder made hanging works whose parts shift with the slightest breath, and the ready-made word for anything movable was borrowed to name the genre.
senses.whyCN: 雕塑家考尔德做了许多悬挂作品，部件随最轻的气流改变位置，于是那个现成的「可动之物」被借来给这类作品命名。

intro.en: Mobile is Latin mobilis, able to move, built on the verb movere, and English took it through French before applying it to phones and to hanging sculptures.
intro.cn: mobile 是拉丁语 mobilis（能移动的），由动词 movere（移动）构成；英语经法语借入，后来才用于手机与悬挂雕塑。

items.en: Movere meant to move, to set in motion or to stir, and it stands behind a large family of English words about motion.
items.cn: movere 意为移动、使动起来、搅动，英语里一大族与运动有关的词都出自它。

items.en: The suffix -bilis turned a verb into an adjective of possibility, so movere plus -bilis gave a word for what can be moved.
items.cn: 后缀 -bilis 把动词变成表示可能性的形容词，于是 movere 加 -bilis 就得出了「能被移动的」这个词。

items.en: Mobilis meant movable and also changeable, and it already described unsettled people and shifting fortune, not only objects.
items.cn: mobilis 既指可移动的，也指易变的，它早就不只用于实物，还用来描述不安定的人和变动不居的命运。

items.en: Old French kept the adjective as mobile, and English borrowed it in the fifteenth century, first in the language of law and natural philosophy.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词保留为 mobile，英语在十五世纪借入，最早用在法律与自然哲学的语言里。

items.en: Modern English added the telephone sense in the late twentieth century and the hanging-sculpture sense in the nineteen thirties, both resting on the same idea of easy movement.
items.cn: 现代英语在二十世纪后期加上了电话义，在一九三〇年代加上了悬挂雕塑义，两者都建立在「容易移动」这一同一个想法上。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb of moving and its adjective; the near-meaning group gathers words for things light enough or free enough to be carried about.
note.cn: 形近组顺着拉丁语「移动」动词及其形容词展开；近义组收表示「轻便得可以随身带走」的词。

entries.definition: The ability to move or to change position or job.
entries.definitionCN: 移动或更换位置、工作的能力。

entries.definition: A car, literally a self-moving vehicle.
entries.definitionCN: 汽车，字面是「自己会动的交通工具」。

entries.definition: Unable to move; fixed in place.

entries.definition: Light and small enough to carry with you.

entries.definition: Able to be shifted from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 能从一处移到另一处的。

entries.definition: Able to be carried or shipped from place to place.

normalIntro.en: The word descends from the Latin verb to move, and its family keeps splitting into what can be shifted, who can move up, and the device that travels with a person.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词出自拉丁语「移动」的动词，同族词不断分成三类：能被挪动的东西、能向上流动的人，以及跟着人走的设备。

normal.en: Movere is the Latin verb to move, and its family spreads across English in mobile, motion, motor, remove and promote.
normal.cn: movere 是拉丁语「移动」的动词，它的词族铺满英语，见于 mobile、motion、motor、remove 与 promote。

normal.en: -bilis marks what can be done, so mobilis is not merely moving but movable, and immobile is its negated twin.
normal.cn: -bilis 标记「可以做到的」，所以 mobilis 不只是「动」，而是「可被移动」；immobile 则是它的否定对应。

normal.en: The noun dropped phone and kept the adjective: a mobile is a telephone defined by its freedom from a fixed line.
normal.cn: 名词省掉了 phone，只留下形容词：a mobile 就是靠「不拴在固定线路上」来定义的一部电话。

normal.en: Mobility adds -ity to mobile and turns the ability to move into a measurable social fact.
normal.cn: mobility 在 mobile 后加 -ity，把「能移动」变成一项可以衡量的社会事实。

normal.en: Calder's hanging works were called mobiles because they move, a young sense resting on the oldest core of the word.
normal.cn: 考尔德的悬挂作品被称为 mobile，因为它们会动；这个年轻的义项仍立足于这个词最老的核心。

abstract.en: Picture a suitcase with wheels: the same object stays whole while its place keeps changing.
abstract.cn: 想象一只带轮子的箱子：东西还是那件东西，位置却一直在换。

abstract.en: A word for easy movement ends up naming a phone, a workforce and a work of art, because all three refuse to stay fixed.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「容易移动」的词最后指手机、劳动力和一件艺术品，因为这三者都不肯固定不动。

abstract.en: What can be moved can also be re-ranked, so physical mobility quietly turns into social mobility.
abstract.cn: 能被搬动的东西也能被重新排位，于是身体的移动悄悄变成了社会地位的流动。

examples.en: A mobile desk lets you work in either room.
examples.cn: 一张可移动的书桌让你在哪个房间都能工作。

examples.en: She answered her mobile while dragging a suitcase through the crowd.
examples.cn: 她一边拖着行李箱穿过人群，一边接听手机。

examples.en: The gallery hung a large mobile above the stairs.
examples.cn: 画廊在楼梯上方挂了一件大型活动雕塑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「谋拜偶」——举着手机四处谋生，走到哪儿拜到哪儿；记住 mobile 是可移动的，也指手机与活动雕塑。

root: 拉丁语 movere（移动）加后缀 -bilis（能……的）构成 mobilis（可移动的），经古法语 mobile 进入英语；同族词有 mobility、mobilize、automobile、immobile。

sensesIntro.en: The core is easy movement; the senses divide into things that can be shifted, people who change rank, the phone in a pocket, and the sculpture that turns in the air.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「容易移动」；义项由此分出能被挪动的东西、能换地位的人、口袋里的手机，以及在空中转动的雕塑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wheeled case that stays whole while its place keeps changing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只带轮子的箱子，东西不变，位置一直在换。

branches.cn: 一张书桌被从一间房推到另一间房

branches.en: a handset lifted to an ear on a crowded platform
branches.cn: 拥挤站台上举到耳边的一部手机

branches.en: metal arms turning slowly above a bed
branches.cn: 病床上方缓缓转动的金属臂

branches.en: one word for the worker who moves and the phone that moves with him
branches.cn: 同一个词，既指流动的工人，也指跟着他走的手机

latinIntro.en: Latin movere and its adjective mobilis supply the whole family, while motus and motor name the movement and the one who moves.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的 movere 及其形容词 mobilis 支撑起整个词族，motus 与 motor 则分别指运动与推动者。

definition_en: the amount that something can hold, or the ability to do something
core_image: 一个容器被慢慢灌满，液面升到边缘
scene: 这个水箱能装下一百升水。 The tank has a capacity of one hundred litres.

senses.title: The amount a container can hold
senses.definition: the maximum amount that a container, room, or vehicle can hold
senses.definitionCN: 容器、空间或交通工具最多能装下的量
senses.example: The hall has a seating capacity of five hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 这个大厅能容纳五百人就座。
senses.why: Latin capax meant able to hold, so the noun first named how much could be held.

senses.title: The ability to do or understand something

senses.title: The maximum amount a factory can produce

senses.why: A production line is treated as a container too: capacity is how much output it can hold.
senses.whyCN: 生产线也被当成容器：capacity 就是它能盛下多少产出。

intro.en: Capacity is the noun of holding: it comes from the Latin adjective for roomy.
intro.cn: capacity 是「容纳」的名词形式，来自拉丁语中表示「能装」的形容词。

items.en: capax meant able to hold or roomy, built on capere, to take or hold.
items.cn: capax 意为「能容纳的、宽敞的」，建立在 capere（拿、容纳）之上。

items.en: capacitas turned that adjective into a noun naming the power to hold.
items.cn: capacitas 把这个形容词变成名词，指「容纳的能力」。

items.en: The noun entered Old French as capacité, keeping the sense of room and ability.
items.cn: 这个名词以 capacité 进入古法语，保留「空间」与「能力」两重意思。

items.en: English borrowed it for the volume a vessel could contain.
items.cn: 英语借入它，用来指容器可容纳的体积。

items.en: The sense widened to mental ability and then to industrial output.
items.cn: 词义先扩展到心智能力，再扩展到工业产出。

note.en: Capacity shares the root capere with capable, and it sits beside other measures of size and power.
note.cn: capacity 与 capable 共享词根 capere，同时和别的「大小、能力」度量词相邻。

senses.title: A baked dish with a pastry crust
senses.definition: a baked food consisting of a pastry crust that encloses a filling of meat, fruit, or vegetables
senses.definitionCN: 一种烤制的食物，酥皮外壳包裹着肉、水果或蔬菜做成的内馅
senses.example: She baked an apple pie for the family dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 她为家庭晚餐烤了一个苹果派。
senses.why: The core image is a crust that completely wraps the filling, so the word first names the wrapped whole rather than the contents.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是酥皮把内馅整个包住，所以这个词首先指「包住的整体」，而不是里面的馅料。

senses.title: A sweet dessert pie
senses.definition: a pie whose filling is sweet, made with fruit, custard, or cream, served as dessert
senses.definitionCN: 内馅为甜味的派，用水果、蛋奶冻或奶油做成，作为甜点食用
senses.example: For dessert we had cherry pie with ice cream.
senses.exampleCN: 甜点我们吃了樱桃派配冰淇淋。
senses.why: Once the pastry whole is the concept, the filling distinguishes subtypes, and sweet fillings became the default image in American English.
senses.whyCN: 既然「酥皮整体」已是概念核心，内馅便用来区分小类；甜馅在美式英语中成了默认画面，于是甜派独立成一个常用义项。

senses.title: A savoury meat pie
senses.definition: a pie filled with meat, gravy, or vegetables, eaten as a main dish or snack
senses.definitionCN: 以肉、肉汁或蔬菜为馅的派，可当主食或点心
senses.example: He bought a hot meat pie at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他在车站买了一个热乎的肉馅饼。
senses.why: The same wrapped-whole image works for savoury fillings, and this is the older, especially British, everyday sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 「包裹的整体」这一意象同样适用于咸馅；咸派是这个词更古老、尤其在英国更日常的义项。

senses.title: A whole divided into shares
senses.definition: something regarded as a whole amount of money, power, or benefit that can be divided among people
senses.definitionCN: 被看作一笔钱、一份权力或一批好处，可以在人们之间切分的整体
senses.example: Both firms want a bigger slice of the profit pie.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司都想从利润这块大蛋糕里分到更大的一块。
senses.why: A round pie is naturally cut into slices, so the image extends to any whole whose parts are shares fought over by claimants.
senses.whyCN: 圆派天然要切成块，这一画面便延伸到任何可以被切分、且各方争抢份额的整体，如利润、市场或预算。

senses.title: A circular statistical diagram
senses.definition: a circle divided into sectors, each showing the proportion of one part of a whole, as in a pie chart
senses.definitionCN: 被分成若干扇形的圆，每个扇形表示整体中某一部分所占比例，用于饼图
senses.example: The report shows spending in a pie chart.
senses.exampleCN: 报告用饼图展示了各项支出。
senses.why: Because the divided-pie image already means a whole split into shares, statisticians borrowed it for a circle cut into proportional sectors.
senses.whyCN: 既然「切分的派」已表示「整体分成份额」，统计学家便借用了这幅画面，把分成比例扇形的圆叫作饼图。

senses.title: Something very easy
senses.definition: something very easy to do, as in the informal phrase as easy as pie
senses.definitionCN: 非常容易做到的事，见于非正式短语 as easy as pie（易如反掌）
senses.example: Don't worry, the test is as easy as pie.
senses.exampleCN: 别担心，这次考试易如反掌。
senses.why: Eating a pie is pleasant and takes no skill, so the phrase came to describe tasks as effortless as enjoying dessert.
senses.whyCN: 吃派轻松愉快、不需要任何技巧，于是这个说法被用来形容像吃甜点一样毫不费劲的任务。

senses.title: A false or empty promise
senses.definition: a promised benefit that is unrealistic and will never arrive, as in pie in the sky
senses.definitionCN: 不切实际、永远不会兑现的许诺，见于短语 pie in the sky（空中馅饼；空头支票）
senses.example: Their pledge of free housing is just pie in the sky.
senses.exampleCN: 他们免费住房的承诺不过是空中馅饼。
senses.why: A pie floating in the sky can be seen but never eaten, so the image names a reward that is dangled yet permanently out of reach.
senses.whyCN: 挂在天上的派看得见却永远吃不着，这幅画面正好用来命名那种被许诺出来、却始终够不到的好处。

senses.title: An affectionate term for a person
senses.definition: used affectionately of a person one loves, as in sweetie pie or cutie pie
senses.definitionCN: 用于亲昵称呼所爱的人，如 sweetie pie、cutie pie（甜心、宝贝）
senses.example: Come here, sweetie pie, and give me a hug.
senses.exampleCN: 过来，小甜心，抱一个。
senses.why: Something sweet and whole and shared within the family becomes a metaphor for a beloved person, sweet as dessert and dear as home.
senses.whyCN: 甜的、圆满的、全家人分享的东西，被用来比喻所爱的人：像甜点一样甜，像家常一样亲。

intro.en: The word pie was first recorded in English in the late 13th century as a name for the pastry dish, but its ultimate origin is uncertain; the most discussed theory links it to the bird name pie (magpie), from Latin pica.
intro.cn: pie 一词在十三世纪末的英语中首次被记录为这种酥皮点心的名称，但其最终来源不确定；被讨论最多的一种假说是把它与鸟名 pie（喜鹊）联系起来，该鸟名来自拉丁语 pica。

items.en: First attested as 'pie', a pastry case with a filling; the earliest records give no derivation, so the source is generally treated as uncertain.
items.cn: 最早以 pie 的形式出现，指带馅的酥皮点心；最早期的文献没有给出词源说明，因此一般认为来源不确定。

items.en: The bird name pie (as in magpie) goes back to Latin pica 'magpie'; some scholars suggest the dish was named after the bird because its assorted fillings resembled the magpie's habit of collecting all kinds of things, though this link is not proven.
items.cn: 鸟名 pie（见 magpie）可追溯到拉丁语 pica「喜鹊」；一些学者认为点心因馅料五花八门、像喜鹊什么都收集而得名，但这一联系并未被证实。

items.en: Early recipes describe pies as pastry coffins enclosing meat, fish, or fruit, confirming that the defining idea was the enclosing crust rather than any particular ingredient.
items.cn: 早期食谱把派描述为包裹肉、鱼或水果的「酥皮棺盒」，说明其定义性特征是包裹用的酥皮，而非某种特定馅料。

items.en: Figurative uses spread: the divided pie as an image of shared benefits, and the phrase humble pie, a folk-etymological reshaping of 'umble pie' made from offal.
items.cn: 比喻用法扩展：被切分的派成为分享利益的意象；humble pie 则是由 umble pie（用内脏做的派）经民间词源改造而来。

items.en: Compounds and idioms consolidated: pie chart (20th c.), pie in the sky (from a 1911 labour song), as easy as pie, and sweetie pie as a term of endearment.
items.cn: 复合词与习语定型：pie chart（二十世纪）、pie in the sky（出自一九一一年的劳工歌曲）、as easy as pie，以及用作爱称的 sweetie pie。

note.en: Watch out for the short-vowel words that look or sound like pie, and for the pastry words that share its meaning field.
note.cn: 注意与 pie 拼写或发音相近的短元音词，以及与它同处「糕点」义场的词。
