entries.definitionCN: 喜鹊；由 mag 加 pie 构成的复合词，被认为是 pie 的可能词源线索

entries.definition: an open pastry case with a filling but no top crust
entries.definitionCN: 果馅饼；挞；与 pie 同类，但通常无上层酥皮

entries.definition: dough made of flour, fat and water used as the base or covering of baked foods
entries.definitionCN: 油酥面团；酥皮糕点；pie 的外壳正是用 pastry 做的

entries.definition: an open savoury flan of pastry filled with eggs, cream and other foods
entries.definitionCN: 法式咸派（乳蛋饼）；义场与咸派相近

entries.definition: a sweet baked food made from flour, sugar and eggs
entries.definitionCN: 蛋糕；同为甜烤食品，但无酥皮包裹内馅的结构

entries.definition: a dish of food cooked slowly in a covered pot, or the covered pot itself
entries.definitionCN: 砂锅炖菜；同为「包裹式」的家常整份食物，但用锅而非酥皮

normalIntro.en: Five memory hooks built on the word's sounds, compounds and idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 五个记忆钩子，建立在发音、复合词与习语之上。

normal.en: pie /paɪ/ rhymes with 'buy': you buy a pie at the bakery.
normal.cn: pie 与 buy 押韵：在面包店 buy（买）一块 pie（派）。

normal.en: magpie keeps the ending pie: the bird that collects everything, like a pie collecting all kinds of fillings.
normal.cn: magpie（喜鹊）以 pie 结尾：什么都收集的鸟，正如派什么馅都装。

normal.en: pie chart: a circle cut like a pie, each slice a percentage.
normal.cn: pie chart（饼图）：把圆像派一样切开，每块是一个百分比。

normal.en: as easy as pie: eating pie takes no skill, so the task is effortless.
normal.cn: as easy as pie：吃派毫不费劲，所以事情易如反掌。

normal.en: a slice of the pie: profits are the pie, your share is one slice.
normal.cn: a slice of the pie：利润是整张派，你的份额是其中一块。

abstract.en: Picture a golden crust as a lid that seals a treasure of filling underneath.
abstract.cn: 把金黄酥皮想成一个盖子，封住下面满满一盆宝藏般的内馅。

abstract.en: See the whole pie as a coin of benefit: whoever holds the knife decides who eats.
abstract.cn: 把整张派想象成一枚利益硬币：谁握着刀，谁就决定谁有得吃。

abstract.en: Imagine a pie floating in the sky: you can see it, but you can never bite it — a promise that never lands.
abstract.cn: 想象一块派漂在天上：看得见却咬不着——一个永远不会落地的承诺。

examples.en: Mom baked an apple pie and the whole house smelled of cinnamon.
examples.cn: 妈妈烤了一个苹果派，满屋子都是肉桂的香气。

examples.en: The engineers demanded a fair share of the bonus pie.
examples.cn: 工程师们要求在奖金这块蛋糕里分得公平的一块。

examples.en: The budget is shown as a pie chart on the second page.
examples.cn: 预算在第二页用一张饼图来展示。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派」——pie 的发音正像中文的「派」：一块圆饼切开分派给大家，谁都得「派」一块；分派、派送的画面帮助锁定「可分的整体」这层意思。

root: 来源不确定。一般认为 pie 首见于十三世纪末的中古英语，指带馅的酥皮点心；最常见的假说是与鸟名 pie（见 magpie，源自拉丁语 pica「喜鹊」）有关——因派的馅料五花八门，类似喜鹊什么都收集的习性，但此说未被证实，应视为存疑的联想而非定论。

sensesIntro.en: From the concrete pastry whole, the word extends to its sweet and savoury subtypes, then figuratively to any divisible whole, its statistical diagram, and idioms for ease and empty promises.
sensesIntro.cn: 从具体的「酥皮包裹的整份食物」出发，先分出甜、咸两个小类，再比喻为任何可切分的整体，进而延伸到统计图示，以及表示「轻而易举」与「空头许诺」的习语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a golden crust sealing a full filling, cut into slices to be shared
core.cn: 核心意象：金黄酥皮封住满满内馅，切开分食

branches.en: The baked dish itself: crust plus filling as one whole.
branches.cn: 烤制的食物本身：酥皮加内馅构成一个整体。

branches.en: The filling decides the subtype: sweet dessert or savoury meat pie.
branches.cn: 内馅决定小类：甜点派或咸味肉派。

branches.en: The pie cut into slices stands for any divisible whole, including the statistical pie chart.
branches.cn: 被切分的派代表任何可分的整体，包括统计上的饼图。

branches.en: Eating pie is easy and sweet, giving the idioms for easy tasks and affectionate names.
branches.cn: 吃派轻松又甜，由此产生形容「易如反掌」的习语和亲昵的爱称。

branches.en: A pie in the sky can be seen but never eaten: the empty promise.
branches.cn: 天上的派看得见吃不着：空头许诺。

intro.en: pie has no certain root or affix of its own; its word family is built almost entirely from compounds and idioms.
intro.cn: pie 本身没有确定的词根或词缀；它的词族几乎全部由复合词和习语构成。

latinIntro.en: The only Latin-shaped lead is pica, the bird name behind magpie, which some scholars connect to the dish — an unproven hypothesis.
latinIntro.cn: 唯一带拉丁色彩的线索是 pica，即 magpie 一词背后的鸟名，有学者把它与这种点心联系起来——但这是未被证实的假说。

items.meaning: a black-and-white bird that collects shiny things; a hoarder
items.meaningCN: 喜鹊；爱收集亮东西的鸟，比喻囤积杂物的人
items.example: She is a magpie for old postcards.
items.exampleCN: 她对旧明信片见一面就收。

items.meaning: the pastry shell of a pie
items.example: Roll the pie crust thin and even.

items.meaning: a sweet pie filled with apples; a symbol of traditional home values
items.meaningCN: 苹果派；美式家庭传统的象征
items.example: Nothing beats warm apple pie with cream.
items.exampleCN: 没什么能比得上热苹果派配奶油。

items.meaning: a savoury pie filled with meat and gravy
items.meaningCN: 肉馅饼；以肉和肉汁为馅的咸派
items.example: He grabbed a meat pie on his way to work.
items.exampleCN: 他上班路上顺手买了个肉馅饼。

items.meaning: a circle divided into sectors showing proportions
items.meaningCN: 饼图；分成扇形以显示比例的圆形统计图
items.example: Draw a pie chart of the monthly costs.
items.exampleCN: 画一张每月开支的饼图。

items.meaning: an empty promise of future rewards
items.example: Higher pay for longer hours is pie in the sky.
items.exampleCN: 工时更长还指望加薪，那是空中馅饼。

items.example: The recipe is as easy as pie.

items.meaning: a term of endearment for a loved person
humiliation, especially having to admit one's error
items.example: He had to eat humble pie and apologise.
items.exampleCN: 他只好低头认错并道歉。

latinEntries.meaning: magpie; proposed but unproven source of the bird name pie
latinEntries.meaningCN: 喜鹊；被提出作为鸟名 pie 的来源，但未经证实
latinEntries.example: Latin pica survives in the scientific name Pica pica for the magpie.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 pica 保留在喜鹊的学名 Pica pica 中。

derivatives.zh: 由 mag 加 pie 构成的复合名词，义为「喜鹊；爱收集杂物的人」
由 sweetie 加 pie 构成的爱称，义为「甜心；宝贝」

definition_en: especially, or in a way that singles out one part of a larger whole
core_image: 一排相同的灯泡里，有一盏被单独调亮
scene: 评审意见先谈整体，再把问题指向其中一处细节。 The review praised the design, particularly the door handles.
sceneCN: 这里指从整体中单举一项（第 2 个义项：具体到某一项）；句意是评论称赞了设计，尤其是门把手；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Especially in degree
senses.definition: more than usual or more than others in degree
senses.definitionCN: 在程度上超过平常或超过其他
senses.example: The winter was particularly harsh in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 北方的冬天格外严酷。
senses.why: Modifying an adjective, it raises the degree and invites a comparison with other times or places.
senses.whyCN: 修饰形容词时，它抬高程度，并引出与其他时间或地点的比较。

senses.title: In particular
senses.definition: used to single out one part of a larger whole
senses.definitionCN: 用来从较大的整体中单举一部分
senses.example: The report discusses costs, particularly labour costs.
senses.exampleCN: 报告讨论了成本，尤其是人力成本。
senses.why: Here the word narrows a general category to one member, close to specifically.
senses.whyCN: 这里它把一般类别收窄到某一成员，接近「具体地」。

senses.title: Sentence-opening emphasis
senses.definition: placed first to announce the most striking fact
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，宣布最引人注目的事实
senses.example: Particularly striking was the silence in the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 特别引人注目的是大厅里的沉默。
senses.why: The front position turns the highlighted element into the sentence's point of arrival.
senses.whyCN: 句首位置把被强调的成分变成整句的落点。

senses.title: Not particularly
senses.definition: used with not to lower a quality in a polite understatement
senses.definitionCN: 与否定词连用，礼貌地压低某种性质
senses.example: I am not particularly interested in that offer.
senses.exampleCN: 我对那个提议不太感兴趣。
senses.why: The negated form means less than very, a soft refusal rather than a plain no.
senses.whyCN: 否定形式意为「不到很的程度」，是柔和拒绝，而不是直截了当的「不」。

senses.title: Especially given
senses.definition: used before a phrase that strengthens the reasons for a statement
senses.definitionCN: 放在强化理由的短语前
senses.example: The schedule is tight, particularly given the staff shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 日程很紧，尤其考虑到人手不足。
senses.why: The construction adds a factor that makes the claim more forceful, often in argument.
senses.whyCN: 这一结构补上一个使说法更有力的因素，常用于论证。

senses.title: Particularly where or when
senses.definition: used before a clause to mark the case in which a statement matters most
senses.definitionCN: 放在从句前，标出该说法最适用的情形
senses.example: The rule matters particularly when records are shared.
senses.exampleCN: 这条规则在记录被共享时尤其重要。
senses.why: The clause restricts the emphasis to a specific circumstance instead of the whole topic.
senses.whyCN: 从句把强调限制在特定情形上，而不是整个话题。

senses.title: Particularly + noun group
senses.definition: used to single out a group affected by a general statement
senses.definitionCN: 用来单举受一般性说法影响的某一群体
senses.example: The change will affect staff, particularly those near retirement.
senses.exampleCN: 这一改动会影响员工，尤其是临近退休的人。
senses.why: The pattern picks out the subset that carries the main burden.
senses.whyCN: 这一句式挑出承担主要影响的那一子集。

senses.title: Formal written emphasis
senses.definition: in formal prose, a more precise alternative to especially
senses.definitionCN: 在正式散文中，作为「尤其」更精确的替代
senses.example: The findings are particularly relevant to small clinics.
senses.exampleCN: 这些发现对小诊所尤其相关。
senses.why: Formal writing prefers the word when the emphasis is on a specific case rather than a general high degree.
senses.whyCN: 当强调落在具体情形而非一般的「很」时，正式文字更偏爱这个词。

intro.en: Particularly comes from the Latin word for a small part, through its adjective and French, plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「小部分」一词，经形容词与法语，再加英语副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The noun pars, stem part-, means a part or share.
items.cn: 名词词干意为「部分、份额」。

items.en: The diminutive particula means a small part or particle.
items.cn: 指小形式意为「小部分、微粒」。

items.en: The adjective particularis means belonging to a single part or case.
items.cn: 形容词意为「属于某一部分或个别情形的」。

items.en: English particular passes through French and means specific rather than general.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入，意为「特定的」而非「一般的」。

items.en: The adverb adds the usual suffix; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 副词加常见后缀；英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Modern usage separates precise singling out from mere intensity, especially in formal prose.
items.cn: 现代用法把「精确单举」与「单纯加强」分开，正式散文尤其如此。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin small-part stem; the second group contrasts precise singling out with broader degree intensifiers.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「小部分」词干；第二组对照「精确单举」与更宽泛的程度加强词。

entries.definition: Specific rather than general; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 特定而非一般的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: The quality of being specific or detailed.
entries.definitionCN: 特定或详尽的性质。

entries.definition: To state something item by item.
entries.definitionCN: 逐项说明某事。

entries.definition: A very small piece; the same diminutive stem without the adjective ending.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的碎片；同一指小词干，未加形容词词尾。

entries.definition: Above all, or to a high degree; broader because it can simply intensify.
entries.definitionCN: 首先、格外；更宽，因为它可以单纯加强程度。

entries.definition: In a precise and identified way, without the degree sense.
entries.definitionCN: 以精确、指明的方式，不含程度义。

entries.definition: In a way worth noticing; often highlights an example or visible degree.
entries.definitionCN: 以值得注意的方式；常突出例子或可见程度。

entries.definition: The phrase form that singles out one member of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 单举群体中某一成员的短语形式。

entries.definition: More than everything else, ranking first in importance.
entries.definitionCN: 超过其他一切，在重要性上排第一。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real small-part stem and the real split between precision and intensity.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「小部分」词干，并区分「精确」与「强度」。

normal.en: The root is a small part, so the word pulls one piece out of the whole.
normal.cn: 词根是「小部分」，所以它从整体里拉出一块。

normal.en: The report discusses costs, particularly labour costs: that is the word doing its precise work.
normal.cn: 「报告讨论成本，尤其是人力成本」正是这个词在精确单举。

normal.en: Not particularly is a polite way to say not very, not a flat no.
normal.cn: 「不太」是礼貌地说「不是很」，而不是硬邦邦的拒绝。

normal.en: Particularly given adds a reason that makes the claim heavier.
normal.cn: 「尤其考虑到」补上一个让说法更重的理由。

normal.en: In formal prose it often replaces especially when the point is a specific case.
normal.cn: 正式文字里，当重点是具体情形时，它常替代「尤其」。

abstract.en: To be particular is to refuse the comfort of a general statement.
abstract.cn: 「具体」就是拒绝一般性说法带来的舒适。

abstract.en: A bright single lamp changes a row of identical lamps into a picture with a subject.
abstract.cn: 一盏单独调亮的灯，把一排相同的灯变成有主体的画面。

abstract.en: Precision and intensity are different tools, and the word can be either one.
abstract.cn: 精确与强度是两种不同的工具，而这个词两样都能当。

examples.en: The north is particularly cold in January.
examples.cn: 北方在一月格外寒冷。

examples.en: I am not particularly fond of crowded trains.
examples.cn: 我不太喜欢拥挤的火车。

examples.en: The rule was written particularly for small firms.
examples.cn: 这条规则尤其是为小公司写的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「怕提扣了利」——特别怕漏掉某一项，所以单独点出来

root: 拉丁语名词「部分」加指小后缀成「小部分」，再构成形容词「属于个别情形的」；英语经法语借入形容词后加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate degree emphasis, precise singling out, sentence-opening emphasis, negated understatement, added reasons, restricted circumstances, singled-out groups and formal written emphasis.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理程度加强、精确单举、句首强调、否定式低调、补充理由、限定情形、单举群体，以及正式书面强调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lamp in a row turned brighter than all the rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排相同的灯泡里，有一盏被单独调亮。

branches.en: THE DEGREE: more than usual or more than others.
branches.cn: 程度：超过平常或超过其他。

branches.en: THE SINGLED ITEM: one part of a whole, and one affected group.
branches.cn: 单举项：整体中的一部分，以及受影响的某一群体。

branches.en: THE FRONT POSITION: emphasis placed at the head of the sentence.
branches.cn: 前置位置：放在句首的强调。

branches.en: THE SOFT OR STRENGTHENED CLAIM: not particularly lowers, particularly given raises.
branches.cn: 柔化或加强的说法：「不太」压低，「尤其考虑到」抬高。

branches.en: THE RESTRICTED CASE: a circumstance clause and the formal register of precision.
branches.cn: 受限情形：限定情形的从句，以及精确的正式语域。

intro.en: Particularly is a Latin part-noun, a diminutive suffix, an adjective suffix, a French layer and an English adverb suffix.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「部分」名词、指小后缀、形容词后缀、法语层与英语副词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The noun for a part builds a diminutive for a small part, then an adjective for what belongs to one case.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「部分」的名词先构成「小部分」的指小形式，再构成「属于个别情形」的形容词。

items.example: The noun is the general idea of a piece of a whole.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是「整体中的一块」这一总概念。

items.example: The suffix shrinks a part into a small piece.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「部分」缩成小块。

items.example: The small part is the base of the adjective.
The suffix turns the small part into an adjective of belonging.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「小部分」变成表归属的形容词。

items.example: The adjective separates one case from the general class.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把个别情形从一般类别中分出。

items.example: English keeps the adjective for a precise case.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留这个形容词指精确的个别情形。

items.example: The noun names the quality of being specific.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名「具体」这一性质。

items.example: The verb turns precision into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把「精确」变成动作。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into an emphasis adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成强调副词。

definition_en: a child's word for father; an informal or affectionate name for one's father
core_image: 小孩伸手要抱的那个人：家里最让孩子安心的大个子
scene: 小女孩在游乐场摔倒了，眼泪汪汪地张开双臂跑向栏杆外。" Daddy, pick me up!" she cried, running toward the fence.
sceneCN: 这里 daddy 是「爸爸、爹地」（第 1 个义项：孩子对父亲的亲昵称呼）；句意是小女孩哭着喊爸爸来抱她。

pos.zh: 爸爸；爹地（儿语、亲昵称呼）

collocations.zh: 爸爸的小棉袄；最受宠的女儿

derivatives.zh: 由儿语叠词截短而来，义为「爸爸」，比 daddy 稍正式
标准称呼「父亲」，与儿语 daddy 相对
由 daddy 加形容词后缀 -ish 构成，义为「爸爸似的」

senses.title: A child's affectionate word for father
senses.definition: the word children use to talk to or about their father
senses.definitionCN: 孩子用来称呼自己父亲的词，语气亲昵
senses.example: Daddy will read you a story tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚爸爸会给你读一个故事。
senses.why: The doubled syllable -dy is baby talk, softening the adult word into something small and safe.
senses.whyCN: 叠音 -dy 是典型的儿语构形，把成人的「父亲」软化成孩子口中的亲昵称呼。

senses.title: An informal affectionate address to any older man or figure
senses.definition: informal use for a protective or beloved male figure, sometimes playfully
senses.definitionCN: 口语中对有保护意味或深受爱戴的男性角色的昵称，常带玩笑色彩
senses.example: Thanks for fixing my laptop, daddy!
senses.exampleCN: 谢谢你帮我修电脑，老爸！
senses.why: The protective image of a father extends playfully to anyone who takes care of you.
senses.whyCN: 「父亲是保护者」的画面被扩展到任何照顾你的人身上，成为一种玩笑式的亲昵。

senses.title: A dominant or authoritative male figure
senses.definition: informal slang for a man who is the biggest, oldest, or most dominant of his kind
senses.definitionCN: 俚语中指某一类里最大、最老资格或最具支配地位的人物
senses.example: This old truck is the daddy of all off-road vehicles.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆老卡车是所有越野车里的大佬。
senses.why: The family image of the biggest, strongest person in the house maps onto the biggest of any class.
senses.whyCN: 家里「最大最强的人」的画面映射到同类事物中「最大的那个」，成为俚语用法。

intro.en: Daddy belongs to the family of nursery words for parents, formed by doubling a simple syllable.
intro.cn: daddy 属于儿语里称呼父母的词族，通过叠用简单音节构成。

items.en: Generally traced to the earliest syllables infants produce, such as *da or similar velar/bilabial babble; a reconstructed form that arose independently in nearly all languages.
items.cn: 一般认为来自婴幼儿最早发出的音节 *da 一类的声音，重构形式，世界语言中普遍独立产生。

items.en: Old English used fæder as the standard word for father; the baby-talk form dad existed alongside it from an early period.
items.cn: 古英语的标准词是 fæder「父亲」，儿语形式的 dad 很早便与之并行存在。

items.en: The diminutive form daddy, with the affectionate suffix -y, is first recorded around the early 16th century.
items.cn: 带亲昵后缀 -y 的 daddy 约在十六世纪初首次见于记录。

items.en: The word spread through family speech and children's literature, staying firmly informal.
items.cn: 该词通过家庭用语和儿童文学传播，始终保持口语色彩。

items.en: Modern usage keeps daddy as a child's word, while slang extends it to dominant figures and machines.
items.cn: 现代用法中 daddy 主要是孩子的称呼，俚语里还扩展出「大佬、主导者」的用法。

note.en: Daddy is easy to confuse with its plain parent word dad and with father, and with look-alike words in other languages.
note.cn: daddy 容易与它的基础词 dad、标准词 father 混淆，也要注意与其他语言里拼写相近的词区分。

entries.definition: informal word for father, less childish than daddy
entries.definitionCN: 「爸爸」，同样口语，但不如 daddy 幼儿化，是 daddy 截短的基础词

entries.definition: the standard, formal word for a male parent
entries.definitionCN: 「父亲」的标准正式说法；与儿语 daddy 同指一人但语域完全不同

entries.definition: a crane fly or harvestman with very long thin legs
entries.definitionCN: 「盲蛛；大蚊」，一种长着细长腿的昆虫；与 daddy 共用开头但指虫不指人

entries.definition: another affectionate child's word for father, from French
entries.definitionCN: 「爸爸」的另一种儿语说法，源自法语，语感比 daddy 略旧

entries.definition: a short informal form for father, rural or old-fashioned
entries.definitionCN: 「爸」的极简口语形式，带乡村或旧式色彩

entries.definition: informal American word for father
entries.definitionCN: 美式口语「老爸」，与 daddy 同为亲昵非正式称呼

normalIntro.en: Build daddy from its family and sound shape.
normalIntro.cn: 用词族和声音形态记住 daddy。

normal.en: dad + -y: the affectionate suffix turns dad into the childish daddy.
normal.cn: dad 加亲昵后缀 -y，就成了更幼儿化的 daddy。

normal.en: The double d mirrors other nursery words: mommy, doggy, kitty.
normal.cn: 双写 d 与 mommy、doggy、kitty 一样，是典型儿语叠音。

normal.en: Plural daddies keeps the baby-talk pattern of ladies, puppies.
normal.cn: 复数 daddies 的变音和 ladies、puppies 一致，符合儿语规律。

normal.en: Compare family: dad, daddy, father — from casual to formal.
normal.cn: 词族排序：dad、daddy、father，从随意到正式。

normal.en: Sound cue: /ˈdæ/ repeats twice, easy for a toddler to say.
normal.cn: 读音 /ˈdædi/ 的音节重复，正是幼儿最容易发出的音。

abstract.en: Picture small arms reaching up toward a tall figure at the door.
abstract.cn: 想象门口那个高大的身影，小手臂高高举起要抱抱。

abstract.en: Feel the soft double thump of two d's, like a child patting twice.
abstract.cn: 感受两个 d 的柔软双重音，像孩子拍两下手。

abstract.en: Hear a bedtime voice saying the word slowly and warmly.
abstract.cn: 耳边响起睡前温柔缓慢喊出的那个称呼。

examples.en: Daddy promised to take us to the beach on Sunday.
examples.cn: 爸爸答应周日带我们去海边。

examples.en: The little girl drew a picture of mommy and daddy holding hands.
examples.cn: 小女孩画了一幅妈妈和爸爸手牵手的画。

examples.en: Among collectors, this rare stamp is the daddy of them all.
examples.cn: 在收藏家眼里，这枚珍稀邮票是所有邮票中的老大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爹地」——发音几乎就是中文的「爹地」，孩子奶声奶气喊的那声「爹地」就是 daddy，无需另造联想。

root: 儿语叠词：dad（儿语「爸爸」，一般认为源自幼儿最早发出的音节，属重构形式）+ 亲昵后缀 -y；与 fæder（古英语「父亲」）并行而非其派生，标准词 father 另有日耳曼语源。

sensesIntro.en: From the nursery address to father, the word stretches playfully to any protector and then to the biggest of a kind.
sensesIntro.cn: 从孩子对父亲的称呼出发，玩笑式地扩展到任何保护者，再引申为同类中的「最大者、大佬」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the small child's word for the tall protector of the house
core.cn: 核心意象：孩子口中对家中高大保护者的称呼

branches.en: the nursery word itself
branches.cn: 儿语称呼本身

branches.en: affection extends beyond the family
branches.cn: 亲昵称呼溢出家庭范围

branches.en: playful address to a helper or protector
branches.cn: 对帮助者、保护者的玩笑称呼

branches.en: the biggest and oldest of a class
branches.cn: 同类中最大最老资格者

branches.en: slang for dominance in machines or things
branches.cn: 俚语中指机器、事物的「老大」

intro.en: Daddy is built from a nursery base plus the affectionate suffix -y; its family shows how English makes diminutives.
intro.cn: daddy 由儿语词基加亲昵后缀 -y 构成；它的词族展示了英语如何构造小称形式。

latinIntro.en: Daddy has no Latin ancestry; the -y suffix descends from Old English rather than Latin, so no Latin relatives are listed.
latinIntro.cn: daddy 没有拉丁语来源；后缀 -y 出自古英语而非拉丁语，因此不列拉丁同族词。

items.meaningCN: 儿语「爸爸」，daddy 的基础词
亲昵小称后缀，表示「小、可爱、幼儿化」
items.exampleCN: 小狗、小猫、宝宝，同用 -y 后缀

items.meaningCN: 与 daddy 平行的「妈妈」儿语形式

items.example: The daddies watched the school play.
items.exampleCN: 爸爸们观看学校的演出。

items.meaningCN: 「盲蛛；大蚊」复合词，借 daddy 的口语色彩
items.example: A daddy longlegs sat on the windowsill.

items.meaningCN: 与儿语相对的标准词「父亲」，来源不同
爸爸似的、有父亲做派的
源自法语的同类儿语词

definition_en: to state the exact meaning of something, or to mark its limits clearly
core_image: 用一条细线把一片地方圈起来
scene: 老师把粉笔放下，让学生在纸上用一句话说清那个词的意思。 The teacher asked us to define the word in one sentence.
sceneCN: 这里 define 指「给…下定义」（第 1 个义项：说明词的确切含义）；句意是老师要我们用一句话说清那个词。

senses.title: State the exact meaning
senses.definition: to say exactly what a word or idea means
senses.definitionCN: 准确说出一个词或概念的含义
senses.example: The teacher asked us to define the word in one sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 老师要我们用一句话说清这个词的意思。
senses.why: A meaning held in the head is not yet shared with anyone.
senses.whyCN: 留在脑子里的意思，还不算和别人共有。

senses.title: Mark the limits of something
senses.definition: to show where the edge or limit of something lies
senses.definitionCN: 指出事物的边缘或限度在哪里
senses.example: A low wall defines the edge of the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 一道矮墙划出了花园的边。
senses.why: To say what a thing is, is also to say what it is not.
senses.whyCN: 说清一样东西是什么，也就说清了它不是什么。

senses.title: Be the mark of a character
senses.definition: to be the quality that clearly marks a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 成为清楚标示人或事物特点的品质
senses.example: Patience defines a good teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心是好老师最鲜明的特点。
senses.why: The line around a thing is what lets us know it again.
senses.whyCN: 把一样东西圈起来的那条线，让我们能再认出它。

intro.en: Define comes from Latin definire, to set a boundary, from de- completely and finis end or limit.
intro.cn: define 来自拉丁语 definire（划定界限），由 de-（彻底）与 finis（终点、界限）组成。

items.en: Finis meant a boundary, the end of a field or of a life.
items.cn: finis 指边界，可以是一块田的尽头，也可以是生命的终点。

items.en: Definire meant to draw the line around a thing.
items.cn: definire 意为绕着一件事物画出界线。

items.en: Definir kept the sense of settling and deciding.
items.cn: definir 保留了确定与裁定的意思。

items.en: English used define for explaining words as well as limits.
items.cn: 英语用它既讲界限，也讲词义。

items.en: Today we define terms, borders, duties and even a style.
items.cn: 如今我们定义术语、边界、职责，甚至一种风格。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the fine ending, and the meaning group moves from naming to making plain.
note.cn: 形近组共用 fine 这个尾巴，近义组则从命名一路走到讲清楚。

entries.definition: clear and not likely to change
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而不易改变的

entries.definition: to refuse openly to obey
entries.definitionCN: 公开拒绝服从

entries.definition: to make something purer or better
entries.definitionCN: 使某物更纯或更好

entries.definition: to say what something is like
entries.definitionCN: 说出某物是什么样子

entries.definition: to name something exactly and clearly
entries.definitionCN: 准确而清楚地指出某事物

entries.definition: to make something easy to understand
entries.definitionCN: 使某事容易理解

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a line drawn in the dirt and end with a word that makes a person known.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从地上画出的一条线开始，落到一个让人被认出的词。

normal.en: A field needs a fence before anyone can say whose it is.
normal.cn: 一块地要先有篱笆，才谈得上是谁的。

normal.en: To define is to draw a circle and then stand outside it to look.
normal.cn: 下定义就是画一个圈，再站到圈外看它。

normal.en: Say what a word means and you have also said what it does not.
normal.cn: 说清一个词的意思，也就说清它不是什么。

normal.en: Patience does not describe a teacher; it defines one.
normal.cn: 耐心不是描述老师，而是标示出老师。

normal.en: Finis is the end, so define puts an end to vagueness.
normal.cn: finis 是终点，所以 define 就是给含糊画上句号。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip tracing a line in dry earth.
abstract.cn: 想象一个指尖在干土上划出一条线。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp held close so one page is bright and the rest is dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯凑得很近，一页亮着，其余都暗。

abstract.en: Picture a name written under a drawing, fixing what it is.
abstract.cn: 想象画下写着一个名字，把画的内容定住。

examples.en: The teacher asked us to define the word in one sentence.
examples.cn: 老师要我们用一句话说清这个词的意思。

examples.en: A low wall defines the edge of the garden.
examples.cn: 一道矮墙划出了花园的边。

examples.en: Patience defines a good teacher.
examples.cn: 耐心是好老师最鲜明的特点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 define 记成「定分」：de 开头，fine 是「精细」，把意思定得精细，就是下定义。

root: 源自拉丁语 definire，由 de-（彻底）与 finis（界限、终点）组成，本义是绕着一块地画出界线；经古法语 definir 进入英语。界线之内是它，界线之外不是它，所以这个词既表示划定范围，也表示说清含义。

sensesIntro.en: From a line around a field, to a line around a word, to the line that marks a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 从圈住一块田的线，到圈住一个词的线，再到标示一个人的那条线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin line drawn around a piece of ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈细线把一块地围起来。

branches.en: The first sense draws the line around a word's meaning.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把线画在一个词的含义周围。

branches.en: The same line, laid on ground, settles a border.
branches.cn: 同样的线落到地上，就定下了边界。

branches.en: Laid on a person, the line marks what is most truly his.
branches.cn: 这条线落到人身上，就标出他最真的那一面。

branches.en: Meaning and border are both made by drawing limits.
branches.cn: 含义与边界都是靠划出限度做成的。

branches.en: Both senses tell us where something begins and ends.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在告诉我们事物从哪里开始、到哪里为止。

intro.en: Define has given English a whole set of words about clear limits: definition, definite and indefinite.
intro.cn: define 给英语送来一整组关于明确界限的词：definition、definite、indefinite。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is finis, a boundary, with the prefix de- meaning completely.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 finis（边界），前缀 de- 表示彻底。

items.meaning: to fix the meaning or limit
items.example: The law defines the duty of the owner.
items.exampleCN: 法律界定了业主的责任。

items.example: The definition was short and exact.

items.exampleCN: 我们需要一个明确的答复。

items.example: They agreed to an indefinite wait.

items.meaning: to define again in a new way
items.exampleCN: 这场战争重新划定了边界。
这项任务界定得很清楚。

definition_en: when compared with other things of the same kind; to a fairly great degree, though not absolutely
core_image: 两只手把同一块石头举到不同高度的背景前比较大小
scene: 同一块石头，放在不同高度的背景前，看上去大小完全不同。 The room was relatively cheap for the city centre.
sceneCN: 这里 relatively 是「相对地」（第 1 个义项：与同类事物相比而言）；句意为对市中心来说，这个房间相对便宜。画面里可留意：同一块石头在不同背景下的观感。

senses.title: By comparison
senses.definition: when measured against other things of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 与同类事物相比较而言
senses.example: The room was relatively cheap for the city centre.
senses.exampleCN: 对市中心来说，这个房间相对便宜。
senses.why: The adverb keeps the comparison inside the sentence: cheap compared with other rooms, not cheap in itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把比较留在句子内部：与别的房间相比便宜，而不是本身就便宜。

senses.title: Fairly, though not absolutely
senses.definition: to a fairly high degree, with the comparison left understood
senses.definitionCN: 达到相当高的程度，而比较对象被省略
senses.example: The work was finished relatively quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 这项工作完成得相当快。
senses.why: When the other term of the comparison is obvious, the word drifts toward a soft form of very.
senses.whyCN: 当比较的另一方显而易见时，这个词就漂向一种柔和的「很」。

intro.en: Relatively is the adverb of relative, and it keeps the comparison that the adjective implies.
intro.cn: relatively 是 relative 的副词，它保留了形容词所暗示的比较。

items.en: Relatus meant carried back, and what is carried back is always measured against something.
items.cn: relatus 意为被带回的，而被带回之物总是以某物为尺。

items.en: Relativus meant having relation to something else.
items.cn: relativus 意为与其他事物有关的。

items.en: English relative described values that hold only in comparison.
items.cn: 英语 relative 描述只在比较中成立的数值。

items.en: The adverb ending -ly turned the comparison into a way of qualifying a statement.
items.cn: 副词词尾 -ly 把这种比较变成限定陈述的方式。

items.en: Modern speech uses the adverb to soften a claim that would be too strong if stated flatly.
items.cn: 现代口语用这个副词来缓冲一个说得太满的论断。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same comparison family; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of degree and comparison.
note.cn: 形近组收同一比较词族的词；近义组收表程度与比较的副词。

entries.definition: Compared, not absolute.
entries.definitionCN: 相对的。

entries.definition: The state of being relative.
entries.definitionCN: 相对性；相对论。

entries.definition: A connection.
entries.definitionCN: 关系。

entries.definition: When compared with others.
entries.definitionCN: 比较地。

entries.definition: To a moderately high degree.
entries.definitionCN: 相当；还算。

entries.definition: To a certain degree.
entries.definitionCN: 相当；有点。

entries.definition: To a small degree.
entries.definitionCN: 有点；稍微。

normalIntro.en: The adverb warns the reader that a comparison is being made, even when the other side of it stays silent.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词提醒读者：这里正在做比较，即使比较的另一方没有说出口。

normal.en: Relatively cheap means cheap next to the other ones.
normal.cn: relatively cheap 指与别的相比便宜。

normal.en: Relatively speaking is the phrase that makes the comparison explicit.
normal.cn: relatively speaking 是把比较说清楚的那个短语。

normal.en: Relatively few means fewer than you might expect here.
normal.cn: relatively few 指比你在这种情况下预期的要少。

normal.en: The word softens a claim without withdrawing it.
normal.cn: 这个词软化论断，但不撤回论断。

normal.en: Drop the comparison and the sentence may become false.
normal.cn: 去掉比较，这句话可能就不成立了。

abstract.en: Every relative judgement borrows its scale from somewhere.
abstract.cn: 每一个相对判断都从某处借来它的尺度。

abstract.en: Relatively is a small word that keeps us honest about context.
abstract.cn: relatively 这个小词让我们对语境保持诚实。

abstract.en: What is relatively safe may still be unsafe enough.
abstract.cn: 相对安全的东西，也可能仍然足够危险。

examples.en: The room was relatively cheap for the city centre.
examples.cn: 对市中心来说，这个房间相对便宜。

examples.en: The work was finished relatively quickly.
examples.cn: 这项工作完成得相当快。

examples.en: Relatively few students chose the harder course.
examples.cn: 相对较少的学生选了那门更难的课。

dict_mnemonic.text: relative（相对的）加 ly：把「跟谁比」这句话塞进一个副词里，就是「相对地」；比较对象省略时，就成了「相当」。

root: 拉丁 relatus（被带回的）→ relativus（有关的）→ 英语 relative ＋ -ly → relatively；与 relative、relativity、relation 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an implied comparison; the senses move from a comparison that is stated, to a softened degree word when the comparison is understood.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「隐含的比较」；义项从明说的比较，到比较对象被省略时的缓和程度词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one stone shown against backgrounds of different heights, seeming to change size.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手把同一块石头举到不同背景前比较大小。

branches.en: a rent that is low for the area
branches.cn: 在这个地段算低的房租

branches.en: work done faster than expected
branches.cn: 比预期完成得更快的工作

branches.en: a comparison made and a degree implied
branches.cn: 明做的比较与暗示的程度

branches.en: a claim that stops short of very
branches.cn: 没有说到「很」的论断

branches.en: a price judged only against neighbours
branches.cn: 只与邻近房源比较的价格

intro.en: The adjective of comparison takes the English adverb ending, and the result marks a judgement that depends on a scale.
intro.cn: 表比较的形容词接上英语副词词尾，结果便标记一个依赖尺度的判断。

latinIntro.en: The stem is relativus, having relation to; -ly is the English adverb ending.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是 relativus（与其他事物有关的）；-ly 是英语副词词尾。

definition_zh: 传统的；惯例的；因袭的；习俗的
definition_en: following customs or beliefs handed down from the past
core_image: 老裁缝踩缝纫机：按老样子做衣服
scene: 端午临近，外婆在厨房里包粽子，手法和年轻时一模一样： At the wedding the bride wore a bright red dress in the local traditional style.
sceneCN: 这里 traditional 是「传统的」（第 1 个义项：沿袭旧俗的）；句意是新娘按当地老习俗穿红嫁衣。

derivatives.zh: 由 traditional 加 -ly 构成，义为「传统上；通常」
由 traditional 加 -ism 构成，义为「传统主义；因袭守旧」
由 traditional 加 -ist 构成，义为「传统主义者；守旧者」

senses.title: Following customs handed down from the past
senses.definition: following beliefs or ways of behaving that have existed for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 遵循久已存在的信仰或行为方式
senses.example: The family eats a traditional meal on the last night of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人在年末最后一晚吃传统大餐。
senses.why: The core image is making things the old way, the way the lamp was always lit.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是按老办法行事——就像灯一直被那样点亮。

senses.title: Existing as a long-established custom
senses.definition: existing as part of an established practice rather than a new decision
senses.definitionCN: 作为既定惯例存在，而非新近决定
senses.example: Traditionally, the manager signs the report first.
senses.exampleCN: 按惯例，经理第一个在报告上签字。
senses.why: A custom repeated so often becomes the default way.
senses.whyCN: 习俗重复太多次，便成了默认做法。

senses.title: Unwilling to accept new ways
senses.definition: preferring old ways and resisting change
senses.definitionCN: 偏好旧方式并抗拒改变
senses.example: The school is quite traditional and still uses textbooks only.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校相当守旧，仍然只用纸质教材。
senses.why: Holding the lamp too tightly means refusing any new flame.
senses.whyCN: 把旧灯攥得太紧，就意味着拒绝任何新火。

intro.en: Traditional is the adjective of tradition, built with the Latin-derived suffix -al on traditio, a handing down.
intro.cn: traditional 是 tradition 的形容词形式，在拉丁语来源 traditio（传承）上加形容词后缀 -al 构成。

items.en: traditio meant a handing over or the teachings handed down.
items.cn: 拉丁语 traditio 意为「传承之物」或传承行为。

items.en: traditionalis described things relating to what is handed down.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 traditionalis 描述与传承相关的事物。

items.en: English took both tradition and its adjective from French and Latin.
items.cn: 英语的 tradition 与其形容词均借自法语和拉丁语。

items.en: The adjective settled on customs, dress, medicine, and values.
items.cn: 形容词逐渐用于习俗、服装、医学与价值观。

items.en: The extended sense of resisting change is common in modern usage.
items.cn: 现代用法中「守旧」的引申义十分常见。

note.en: Words that look or sound close to traditional, and words in the established-ways field.
note.cn: 与 traditional 形近音近的词，以及同属既定方式义场的词。

entries.definition: one who strongly defends traditions
entries.definitionCN: 传统主义者；守旧者，traditional 加 -ist 的名词

entries.definition: according to tradition
entries.definitionCN: 传统上；通常，traditional 的副词形式

entries.definition: one who betrays
entries.definitionCN: 叛国者，与 traditional 开头相近，词义相悖

entries.definition: following what is generally accepted
entries.definitionCN: 常规的；符合惯例的，强调被普遍接受

entries.definition: usual according to custom
entries.definitionCN: 通常的；习惯上的，强调习惯性

entries.definition: following the generally accepted beliefs
entries.definitionCN: 正统的；规范的，强调 beliefs 的正统

entries.definition: resisting change
entries.definitionCN: 保守的；守旧的，强调抗拒变化

normalIntro.en: Link the long word to tradition and the -al ending.
normalIntro.cn: 把长词拆成 tradition 加 -al 来记。

normal.en: tradition + al = adjective of tradition
normal.cn: tradition 加 -al 即其形容词形式

normal.en: collocation: traditional culture, traditional medicine
normal.cn: 高频搭配：传统文化、传统医学

normal.en: traditionally = most of the time, by custom
normal.cn: traditionally＝传统上、通常

normal.en: -al turns a noun into an adjective
normal.cn: -al 把名词变成形容词：nation→national 同理

normal.en: traditionalist defends the old ways
normal.cn: traditionalist＝守着老办法的人

abstract.en: The old tailor sewing by the same pattern as his grandfather
abstract.cn: 老裁缝照着祖父的版型缝衣

abstract.en: A lamp lit the same way for a hundred years
abstract.cn: 一盏灯用同一方式点亮了一百年

abstract.en: New wind shakes the window; the room keeps its old light
abstract.cn: 新风吹动窗户，屋里仍留着旧光

examples.en: They prefer traditional Chinese medicine to pills.
examples.cn: 比起药片，他们更信任传统中药。

examples.en: Traditionally, children give their elders a New Year greeting.
examples.cn: 按传统，孩子们要向长辈拜年。

examples.en: His views are a bit too traditional for young readers.
examples.cn: 对年轻读者来说，他的观点有些过于守旧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「传滴信了」——传统的东西一代传一代，像水滴一样信得过：传滴信了→ traditional。词根就是 tradition。

root: 拉丁语 trans- + dare（给）→ traditio「传承之物」+ -al「与……相关的」：与传统之事相关的。

sensesIntro.en: From following inherited customs, the adjective widens to firm conventions and resistance to change.
sensesIntro.cn: 形容词从沿袭旧俗扩展到固定惯例与抗拒变化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the old tailor sewing by grandfather's pattern
core.cn: 核心意象：老裁缝照祖父的版型缝衣

branches.en: ways of doing things inherited from the past
branches.cn: 从过去继承的行事方式

branches.en: the default way when no decision is made
branches.cn: 未做决定时的默认做法

branches.en: refusal of the new in favour of the old
branches.cn: 宁旧勿新的态度

branches.en: custom repeated so long it feels natural
branches.cn: 重复太久以致浑然天成的习俗

branches.en: the default can harden into stubbornness
branches.cn: 默认做法会硬化为固执

intro.en: Traditional keeps the Latin skeleton of tradition and adds the adjective suffix -al.
intro.cn: traditional 保留 tradition 的拉丁骨架，另加形容词后缀 -al。

latinIntro.en: The -al suffix is from Latin -alis, used to make adjectives from nouns.
latinIntro.cn: 后缀 -al 来自拉丁语 -alis，用于由名词构成形容词。

latinEntries.meaning: relating to what is handed down
relating to; of the kind of

definition_zh: 每；每一；按照；根据；经由；由
definition_en: used to show how much of something belongs to each unit, such as each person, hour or kilometre; also according to, and by way of
core_image: 一把量杯上刻着一格一格的刻度，每一格都装着同样多的东西
scene: 清晨的渡口挂着木牌，船夫按人头收过渡费，来一个人收一次。 The ferryman charges five yuan per passenger before the boat leaves the shore.
sceneCN: 这里 per 是「每、每一」（第 1 个义项：按单位逐一计算份量）；句意为开船之前，船夫向每位乘客收五元。画面的重点是刻度式的一份一份。

derivatives.zh: 由 per 与拉丁语 centum（百）组合而成，义为「百分比」
在 percent 后加名词后缀 -age，义为「百分比；比例」
拉丁短语 per capita（按人头）整体进入英语，义为「人均的」

senses.title: For each unit
senses.definition: used to state how much of something corresponds to one person, hour, kilometre or other unit
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明每一个人、每一小时、每一公里等对应多少量
senses.example: The room costs eighty dollars per night.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间每晚八十美元。
senses.why: Latin per already worked in distributive phrases such as per diem, so English simply kept that rhythm: one measured portion for every single unit.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 per 早已用于表示分配的说法，如按日计算，所以英语直接沿用了这种节奏：每一个单位都配一份量。

senses.title: According to
senses.definition: used to mean in accordance with what someone has said, asked for or decided
senses.definitionCN: 表示与某人的说法、要求或决定相一致
senses.example: Per your request, the meeting has been moved to Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 按照你的要求，会议已改到星期五。
senses.why: If something reaches you through a person, that person becomes the source of the instruction, so through slides into according to, the way a message is passed on in an office.
senses.whyCN: 如果一件事是经某个人传到你这儿的，那个人就成了指令的来源，于是「经由」滑向「按照」，就像办公室里逐层转达的口信。

senses.title: By way of
senses.definition: used to name the person or the means through which something is sent, carried or done
senses.definitionCN: 用于指出某物经谁之手、或以什么方式送出、运走或完成
senses.example: The documents were sent per courier.
senses.exampleCN: 这些文件由快递员送出。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of the Latin word: movement through a channel, whether a road, a hand or a service, and English kept it for post, fax and courier.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁词最古老的一层意思：沿着某个通道穿过，通道可以是道路、一只手或一项服务，英语把它保留在邮寄、传真与快递的说法里。

senses.title: In every hundred
senses.definition: used in the phrase per cent to express a rate measured out of one hundred
senses.definitionCN: 用于 per cent 这一短语，表示以一百为基数计算的比率
senses.example: Prices rose by three per cent last month.
senses.exampleCN: 上个月价格上涨了三个百分点。
senses.why: Per cent joins per with Latin centum, a hundred, and the counting frame does the rest: so many units out of every hundred.
senses.whyCN: per cent 把 per 与拉丁语 centum（一百）拼在一起，剩下的交给计数框架完成：每一百当中占多少。

intro.en: Per is a Latin preposition of passage, and English took it over both as a word of route and as a word of counting.
intro.cn: per 是拉丁语中表示穿行的介词，英语既把它当作「路线词」，也把它当作「计数词」接收下来。

items.en: The reconstructed root per- carried the idea of forward motion and passing through, and forms built on it appear in many branches of the family.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 per- 带有「向前、穿过」的意思，由它构成的词形出现在语系的许多分支里。

items.en: Latin per meant through, across or by means of, and it could also mark the person through whom something happened.
items.cn: 拉丁语 per 意为穿过、横越、凭借，也可以标出事情是经谁发生的。

items.en: In phrases such as per diem and per capita, the word moved from place to share, meaning for each day and for each head.
items.cn: 在 per diem、per capita 这类短语里，这个词从「位置」转到「分配」，意为每天、每人。

items.en: English borrowed the counting use first in trade, law and household accounts, where rates were quoted per dozen, per acre and per year.
items.cn: 英语先在贸易、法律与家庭账目里借用这种计数用法，报价写作每打、每英亩、每年。

items.en: Modern English adds as per and per cent, so one small word now marks a rate, a source and a percentage at once.
items.cn: 现代英语又添了 as per 与 per cent，于是同一个小词同时标记比率、来源与百分比。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words and phrases built on the same Latin preposition; the near-meaning group gathers the determiners and prepositions that divide or route things.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一拉丁介词上的词与短语；近义组收表示分配与途径的限定词、介词。

entries.definition: A word for a rate out of a hundred, built from per plus Latin centum.
entries.definitionCN: 由 per 与拉丁语 centum（百）构成的词，表示百分之几。

entries.definition: The two-word British form of the same idea, still common in British writing.
entries.definitionCN: 同一概念的两词英式写法，在英式文本里仍很常见。

entries.definition: To keep going firmly, built on per- plus a Latin verb meaning to stand.
entries.definitionCN: 由 per- 加表示「站立」的拉丁动词构成，义为坚持。

entries.definition: To spread through every part of something, with per- meaning through.
entries.definitionCN: per- 表示穿过，故义为弥漫、遍及。

entries.definition: Every one of two or more things, taken one at a time.
entries.definitionCN: 两个或更多事物中的每一个，逐一来看。

entries.definition: All the members of a group, considered one by one.
entries.definitionCN: 一组中的全部成员，逐个来看。

entries.definition: By going through a place, or by using a particular method.
entries.definitionCN: 经由某地，或使用某种方法。

entries.definition: Used to name the person or the method that does something.
entries.definitionCN: 用于指出做某事的人或方法。

normalIntro.en: Per is a Latin preposition of passage, and every English use keeps either the route or the counting beat built into it.
normalIntro.cn: per 是拉丁语中表示穿行的介词，英语的每种用法都保留了它内含的路线或计数节拍。

normal.en: Per is the Latin word for through, so anything sent per someone passes through that person's hands.
normal.cn: per 在拉丁语里是「穿过」，所以经某人转交的东西要先过那个人的手。

normal.en: Per cent is per plus centum, the Latin word for a hundred: so many in every hundred.
normal.cn: per cent 是 per 加拉丁语 centum（一百），即每一百当中占多少。

normal.en: Per capita joins per with capita, the Latin word for heads: one share for each head.
normal.cn: per capita 把 per 与拉丁语 capita（头）连起来：按人头各分一份。

normal.en: As per is the business formula for according to, and it appears in letters, notices and instructions.
normal.cn: as per 是商业文书里表示「按照」的固定说法，常见于信件、通告与说明。

normal.en: Per hour, per night and per person all keep one frame: a fixed amount repeated for each unit.
normal.cn: per hour、per night、per person 都保持同一个框架：固定的量按单位重复。

abstract.en: A ruler scored with equal spaces is the clearest picture of per: the same amount repeated at every mark.
abstract.cn: 一把刻着等距刻度的尺子最能说明 per：每一格都是同样的量。

abstract.en: The word began as motion through space and ended as a way of splitting amounts, a journey from road to ledger.
abstract.cn: 这个词从空间中的穿行开始，最后成为分配数量的工具，一路从道路走到账簿。

abstract.en: Because per stands between an amount and a unit, it forces the speaker to say what the amount is measured against.
abstract.cn: 因为 per 夹在数量与单位之间，它逼着说话人交代这个量是拿什么来衡量的。

examples.en: The room costs eighty dollars per night.
examples.cn: 这个房间每晚八十美元。

examples.en: Per your request, the meeting has been moved to Friday.
examples.cn: 按照你的要求，会议已改到星期五。

examples.en: Prices rose by three per cent last month.
examples.cn: 上个月价格上涨了三个百分点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼」——一桶水泼出去，每处都沾到一点；用它记住 per 是「每」。

root: 拉丁语介词 per（穿过、经由、每）直接进入英语；同族词多与「穿过、彻底」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a quantity measured against a unit; from that counting frame grow the ideas of source, route and percentage.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「以一个单位为基准的量」；来源、途径与百分比三个意思都从这个计数框架里长出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a measuring cup marked with equal lines, one portion standing for every line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把量杯上刻着一格一格的线，每一条线代表同样的一份。

branches.en: a ticket window that charges by the head
branches.cn: 按人头收费的售票窗口

branches.en: a price tag that shows both a rate and a share
branches.cn: 同时标着单价与百分比的价签

branches.en: a notice that opens with the words of the person who asked
branches.cn: 以对方要求开头的通知

branches.en: a parcel passing from one pair of hands to another
branches.cn: 在一双双手之间转交的包裹

branches.en: a chart that cuts a total into a hundred parts
branches.cn: 把总量切成一百份的图表

intro.en: Per is a Latin preposition of passage; the English forms around it are mostly phrases that share the same counting frame.
intro.cn: per 是拉丁语中表示穿行的介词，围绕它的英语形式多是共用同一计数框架的短语。

latinIntro.en: Both halves of the percentage words come from Latin: per and centum are securely attested and their meanings are not in doubt.
latinIntro.cn: 百分比一族的两半都来自拉丁语：per 与 centum 均有可靠记载，含义没有争议。

items.meaning: a rate out of a hundred
a share expressed out of a hundred

definition_en: a feeling of admiration, or a particular aspect of something
core_image: 一个人后退半步，认真看着对方，身体微微前倾
scene: 那位老教师走进教室时，所有学生都站起来表示敬意。 When the old teacher entered the classroom, every student stood up to show respect.
sceneCN: 这里 respect 是「敬意」（第 1 个义项：对某人怀有的钦佩与重视）；句意：老教师走进教室时，所有学生都站起来表示敬意。

senses.title: Admiration and esteem
senses.definition: a feeling of admiration for someone because of their qualities or achievements
senses.definitionCN: 因某人的品质或成就而钦佩他
senses.example: Every student stood up to show respect.
senses.exampleCN: 每个学生都站起来表示敬意。
senses.why: The Latin word means a looking back at someone, and that look becomes esteem.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词意为回头注视某人，这种注视就变成敬意。

senses.title: A particular aspect
senses.definition: one detail or point in which things can be compared
senses.definitionCN: 事物可以相互比较的某个细节或要点
senses.example: In this respect, the two plans are alike.
senses.exampleCN: 在这方面，两项计划很相似。
senses.why: Looking back at a thing can mean looking at one particular side of it.
senses.whyCN: 「回头看某物」也可以指看它的某一个侧面。

senses.title: To admire and treat well
senses.definition: to admire someone and treat them with care and fairness
senses.definitionCN: 钦佩某人并以体贴、公平的方式对待他
senses.example: She respects her teacher greatly.
senses.exampleCN: 她非常尊敬她的老师。
senses.why: The noun's esteem becomes the verb's way of acting toward someone.
senses.whyCN: 名词的「敬意」变成动词对待某人的方式。

intro.en: Respect comes from Latin respectus, a looking back, from respicere, to look back at, built on re- and specere, to look.
intro.cn: respect 来自拉丁语 respectus（回顾），源于 respicere（回头看），由 re- 与 specere（看）构成。

items.en: Specere means to look at.
items.cn: specere 意为看。

items.en: Respicere means to look back at or consider.
items.cn: respicere 意为回头看、考虑。

items.en: Respectus means a looking back or regard.
items.cn: respectus 意为回顾、注目。

items.en: Respect means regard or consideration.
items.cn: respect 意为重视、考虑。

items.en: Middle English respect covers esteem and a particular point.
items.cn: 中古英语 respect 兼指敬意与某个方面。

items.en: Modern English uses respect as both noun and verb.
items.cn: 现代英语中，respect 兼作名词与动词。

note.en: Respect is a looking-back word, and it sits near its family and near words for esteem and regard.
note.cn: respect 是一个「回头看」的词，与自身词族以及表示敬重和关注的词相邻。

entries.definition: showing respect
entries.definitionCN: 恭敬的；尊重的

entries.definition: in a respectful way
entries.definitionCN: 恭敬地

entries.definition: belonging separately to each one
entries.definitionCN: 各自的

entries.definition: great respect and admiration
entries.definitionCN: 敬重；尊敬

entries.definition: respect or attention for someone
entries.definitionCN: 尊重；关注

entries.definition: public respect or a mark of it
entries.definitionCN: 荣誉；敬意

normalIntro.en: Respect contains specere, to look: respect begins with looking at someone properly.
normalIntro.cn: respect 含有 specere（看）：尊重始于认真注视对方。

normal.en: Re- means back, and specere means look: to look back with regard.
normal.cn: re- 表示回，specere 表示看：带着重视回头看。

normal.en: Show respect is the common phrase.
normal.cn: show respect 是常见短语。

normal.en: In this respect means in this particular aspect.
normal.cn: in this respect 意为「在这方面」。

normal.en: Respectful is the adjective for showing regard.
normal.cn: respectful 是表示「恭敬的」形容词。

normal.en: Compare esteem: esteem is admiration, while respect also includes fair treatment.
normal.cn: 对比 esteem：esteem 是钦佩，respect 还包括公平对待。

abstract.en: Picture a student standing as a teacher enters.
abstract.cn: 想象老师进门时学生站起来。

abstract.en: Imagine a listener putting down the phone to look at you.
abstract.cn: 想象听者放下手机，认真看着你。

abstract.en: Think of a slight bow before a serious conversation.
abstract.cn: 想象严肃谈话前微微躬身。

examples.en: Every student stood up to show respect.
examples.cn: 每个学生都站起来表示敬意。

examples.en: In this respect, the two plans are alike.
examples.cn: 在这方面，两项计划很相似。

examples.en: She respects her teacher greatly.
examples.cn: 她非常尊敬她的老师。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re + spect」——回头再看一眼，是因为心里看重，所以尊重；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 specere（看）→ respicere（回头看）→ respectus（回顾、注目）→ 古法语 respect → 现代英语 respect。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins with a backward look of regard, which becomes esteem, then a particular side of a thing, and finally the way one treats another person.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从带着重视的回头注视开始，变成敬意，再指事物的某个侧面，最后指对待他人的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pausing to look at someone with attention and care.
core.cn: 核心意象：停下来，带着关注与体贴看着某人。

branches.en: Esteem is the feeling produced by that careful look.
branches.cn: 敬意是由认真注视产生的感受。

branches.en: A respect is one side of a thing seen closely.
branches.cn: 「方面」是近距离观察到的某个侧面。

branches.en: The verb turns esteem into fair treatment.
branches.cn: 动词把敬意变成公平对待。

branches.en: Feeling respect and acting respectfully belong together.
branches.cn: 心怀敬意与以礼相待彼此相连。

definition_zh: 投票；表决；选举；投票权；得票数
definition_en: to express your choice in an election or decision by formally marking a ballot or raising a hand
core_image: 举起的手和纸上的勾：把你的选择放进所有人的选择里一起数
scene: 会场安静下来，主持人宣布开始表决。 Every member has one vote in the annual meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 vote 是「投票权」（第 4 个义项：一名成员所拥有的那一份表决权）；句意是年会上每位成员都有一票。

pos.zh: 名词：投票；表决；选票；得票数；投票权
动词：投票；表决；选举；投票通过

名词，义为「选票」，义场相邻的名词

senses.title: To express a formal choice
senses.titleCN: 投票：用规定方式表达选择
senses.definition: to mark a ballot or otherwise formally show whom or what you support
senses.definitionCN: 在选票上做记号或以其他规定方式表明你支持的人或提案
senses.example: Millions of citizens voted in the national election.
senses.exampleCN: 数百万公民在全国大选中投了票。
senses.why: Latin votum means a vow or wish; a formal choice is a wish made publicly and countably.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 votum 意为誓愿；正式的选择就是把愿望公开说出、可以被统计。

senses.title: To decide by collective choice
senses.definition: to reach a group decision by counting everyone's choices
senses.definitionCN: 通过统计每个人的选择来作出集体决定
senses.example: The committee voted to postpone the project.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会表决决定推迟该项目。
senses.why: Many wishes are laid side by side and counted; the largest one becomes the decision.
senses.whyCN: 把众人的愿望并列在一起计数，占多数的那个便成为决定。

senses.title: A single choice cast
senses.definition: an act or piece of paper showing one person's choice in an election
senses.definitionCN: 表明一个人在选举中选择的动作或那张纸
senses.example: She put her vote into the ballot box and left.
senses.exampleCN: 她把选票投入票箱，然后离开。
senses.why: Each wish becomes one unit to be counted; the unit itself is a vote.
senses.whyCN: 每个愿望化作一个可数的单位，这个单位本身就是一张选票。

senses.title: The right to take part
senses.titleCN: 投票权：参与表决的资格
senses.definition: the right that a person or member has to take part in a decision
senses.definitionCN: 个人或成员参与决定所拥有的资格
senses.example: Every member has one vote in the annual meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 年会上每位成员都有一票。
senses.why: If a wish counts, that counting is a right; having one wish means having one vote.
senses.whyCN: 愿望若被统计，这种被统计就是一项权利；有一份愿望即有一票。

senses.title: The total or result counted
senses.titleCN: 得票数：统计出来的总数
senses.definition: the total number of choices recorded in an election or ballot
senses.definitionCN: 选举或表决中记录到的选择总数
senses.example: The final vote gave the mayor a second term.
senses.exampleCN: 最终计票结果让市长获得连任。
senses.why: Counted wishes add up to a number; that number names the outcome.
senses.whyCN: 被计数的愿望累加为数字，这个数字就代表结果。

senses.title: To approve or choose by ballot
senses.titleCN: 投票选出：用投票方式认可或选出
senses.definition: to choose someone or approve something through a formal ballot
senses.definitionCN: 通过正式投票选出某人或通过某事
senses.example: The players voted her captain of the team.
senses.exampleCN: 队员们投票选她当队长。
senses.why: The collective wish is aimed at a person; choosing becomes electing.
senses.whyCN: 集体的愿望指向一个人，选择便成为选举。

intro.en: Vote descends from Latin votum, a vow or solemn wish, the past participle of vovere, to promise solemnly.
intro.cn: vote 源自拉丁语 votum（誓愿、庄重的愿望），它是动词 vovere（郑重许诺）的过去分词。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ewegwh- or a related form means to speak solemnly or vow; the exact shape is generally agreed only within Latin.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根与「郑重言说、许愿」相关，其确切形态仅在拉丁语内部较有共识。

items.en: Vovere means to vow; votum is what is vowed, a wish dedicated to the gods.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vovere 意为许愿；votum 是许下的愿，即献给神明的愿望。

items.en: Votum extends from religious wishes to any solemnly expressed choice or opinion.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语中，votum 从宗教誓愿扩展为任何郑重表达的愿望或意见。

items.en: English takes vote from the Latin participle, first as a solemn wish, then as an expressed opinion.
items.cn: 英语直接取自拉丁语分词形式的 vote，先指庄重的愿望，后指表达出的意见。

items.en: The political sense hardens: a vote becomes a counted choice in parliament and elections.
items.cn: 17 世纪政治义定型：vote 成为议会与选举中可被统计的选择。

items.en: Vote now covers casting ballots, electing leaders, and counting the results in any assembly.
items.cn: 如今 vote 涵盖投票、选人、计票，适用于各种集会与选举。

note.en: Vote belongs to the Latin vow-family and the election word-field; look-alikes share the vow-root or spelling, near meanings share the field of choosing.
note.cn: vote 与拉丁「誓愿」词族及选举义场相邻：形近组共享誓愿词根或拼形，近义组共享「选择」义场。

entries.definition: the power to reject a decision; to reject it
entries.definitionCN: 否决（权）；源自拉丁语，字面为「我不许」，与 vote 同出「愿」词族但方向相反

entries.definition: to give time, love, or energy to something
entries.definitionCN: 奉献、专注于；由 de- 加 vovere 词根构成，义为郑重许下

entries.definition: offered or done as a vow or wish
entries.definitionCN: 还愿的、许愿的；与 vote 同根的形容词，属宗教用词

entries.definition: a paper or system used for voting
entries.definitionCN: 选票、投票制；与 vote 只是义场相接，词源是意大利语的小纸球，拼写易混但词源不同

entries.definition: careful not to confuse vote with veto: one chooses, one rejects
entries.definitionCN: vote 与 veto 仅一字母之差：一个选择，一个否决；devoted 则属同根词，词形相近易混

entries.definition: a system, paper, or act of secret voting
entries.definitionCN: 选票、无记名投票；强调投票的形式

entries.definition: to choose someone for a position by voting
entries.definitionCN: 选举、推选；强调选出人担任职位

entries.definition: the process of voting, or a survey of opinions
entries.definitionCN: 投票；也指民意调查，侧重统计人数

entries.definition: a direct public vote on a single question
entries.definitionCN: 全民公投；针对单一议题的直接投票

entries.definition: to choose not to vote
entries.definitionCN: 弃权；与投票相对的选择

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the Latin vow-family of vovere and votum.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，全部来自拉丁语 vovere（许愿）与 votum（誓愿）词族。

normal.en: vovere means to vow; voting is your wish said out loud and counted.
normal.cn: vovere 意为许愿；投票就是把愿望说出来并被人计数。

normal.en: devote is the same root: to vow yourself to something.
normal.cn: devote 同根：把自己许诺给某事。

normal.en: veto keeps the first-person Latin shape: I forbid, the opposite of choosing.
normal.cn: veto 保留拉丁第一人称形态：我不许，恰是选择的反面。

normal.en: voter is the person who turns a wish into a counted choice.
normal.cn: voter 是把愿望变成一张被计数选票的人。

normal.en: cast a vote is the fixed phrase: throwing your wish onto the pile.
normal.cn: cast a vote 是固定搭配：把你的愿望投进那一堆里。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl where every hand drops one stone: the tallest pile is the decision.
abstract.cn: 想象一只碗，每只手投进一颗石子：堆得最高的那边就是决定。

abstract.en: A wish whispered to a god in Rome becomes a card dropped in a box today.
abstract.cn: 古罗马对神低声许下的愿，如今变成投进箱中的一张卡。

abstract.en: One voice alone is faint; counted together, voices become a verdict.
abstract.cn: 一个声音很微弱，加在一起被计数，声音便成为裁决。

examples.en: Employees voted for a shorter working week.
examples.cn: 员工们投票赞成缩短每周工时。

examples.en: The bill passed by a narrow vote in the senate.
examples.cn: 该法案在参议院以微弱的票数差距获得通过。

examples.en: Who did you vote for in the last election?
examples.cn: 上次选举你投了谁的票？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我投」——vote 的发音就像「我投」，我投出我的一票。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自拉丁 votum（誓愿）。

root: 拉丁语 vovere（郑重许诺、许愿）+ 过去分词 votum（誓愿）进入英语，先义为愿望、意见，后义为投票。同根词 devote（奉献）、devout（虔诚的）、votive（还愿的）同出一族，核心是「郑重表达愿望」。

sensesIntro.en: From one solemn wish to a counted collective verdict: cast it, count it, and the result decides.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一份郑重的愿望到被计数的集体裁决：投出、计数，结果由多数决定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one wish made formal, joined with all wishes and counted
core.cn: 核心意象：一份愿望被正式化，与所有愿望汇合并计数

branches.en: The individual act: one wish formally cast
branches.cn: 个体行为：一份愿望被正式投出

branches.en: The group act: choosing and approving together
branches.cn: 群体行为：共同选择与认可

branches.en: The standing right to be counted
branches.cn: 被计数的资格：投票权

branches.en: The number that the wishes add up to
branches.cn: 愿望累加出的数字：得票数

branches.en: The verdict: from counting to naming a winner
branches.cn: 裁决：从计数到宣布结果

intro.en: The vow-verbs of Latin spread through prefixes that add the wish toward, away, or upward.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的许愿动词借助前缀，把愿望引向不同方向：奉献、转向、许上。

latinIntro.en: In Latin, vovere built a family of words about solemn wishes, sacred or personal.
latinIntro.cn: 在拉丁语中，vovere 构成了一族关于郑重愿望的词，或神圣或个人。

definition_en: to make a serious promise, or to use rude words
core_image: 证人举起手，在法庭上郑重承诺
scene: 他在法庭上发誓说出真相。 He swore to tell the truth in court.
sceneCN: 这里 swear 是「发誓」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他在法庭上发誓说出真相。

senses.title: To make a serious promise
senses.definition: to promise seriously that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 郑重承诺某事为真
senses.example: He swore to tell the truth in court.
senses.exampleCN: 他在法庭上发誓说出真相。
senses.why: This is the core sense of a solemn promise.
senses.whyCN: 这是郑重承诺的核心义项。

senses.title: To take a formal oath
senses.definition: to make a formal promise in a legal or public setting
senses.definitionCN: 在法律或公开场合正式承诺
senses.example: The witness swore an oath before speaking.
senses.exampleCN: 证人在发言前宣了誓。
senses.why: Here the promise is formal and public.
senses.whyCN: 这里承诺是正式而公开的。

senses.title: To use rude words
senses.definition: to speak angrily with offensive words
senses.definitionCN: 用冒犯性词语愤怒地说话
senses.example: He swore loudly when he dropped the box.
senses.exampleCN: 他摔落箱子时大声咒骂。
senses.why: This sense comes from the force of an oath.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来自誓言的力量。

intro.en: Swear is an old Germanic word for taking an oath.
intro.cn: swear 是表示宣誓的古老日耳曼词。

items.en: Swaran meant to swear an oath.
items.cn: swaran 意为宣誓。

items.en: Swerian meant to swear.
items.cn: swerian 意为发誓。

items.en: Swere kept the sense of a solemn promise.
items.cn: swere 保留了郑重承诺之义。

items.en: Swear extended to rude speech.
items.cn: swear 扩展到粗俗言语。

items.en: Sworn became an adjective for formal oaths.
items.cn: sworn 成为描述正式誓言的形容词。

note.en: Swear is compared with look-alike words and with words for promising.
note.cn: 把 swear 与形近词以及表示承诺的词作比较。

abstract.en: An oath asks time to witness what the mouth says now.

core.en: Words bound to honor.
